# ray-elements

> Web components (custom elements, Shadow DOM, no dependencies) for any web app: plain HTML, React, Vue or a raylang app. npm: `@raylang/elements`, `@raylang/react`, `@raylang/vue`; raylang: the `elements` package. This file describes version 0.8.0.

ray-elements is a design system of standard web components (custom elements
with Shadow DOM, no dependencies): `<ray-button>`, `<ray-input>`,
`<ray-dialog>`… They work in plain HTML, React, Vue, a browser or any webview,
and get extras in a raylang app (a native bridge to the program). The rules
below are what this library does differently from what you may assume; the
reference of every component follows them.

## Load it

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="node_modules/@raylang/elements/tokens.css">  <!-- required: the components read the tokens -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="node_modules/@raylang/elements/base.css">    <!-- optional: font, colors and margins of the document -->
<script type="module">
  import "@raylang/elements";          // registers EVERY <ray-*> element and exports the whole API
</script>
```

- The bare name (`"@raylang/elements"`) resolves with a bundler (Vite,
  esbuild…) and in a raylang app (raylang serves the package with an import
  map). A plain page without either imports the files:
  `import { notify } from "./node_modules/@raylang/elements/index.js";`
  (everything), `./node_modules/@raylang/elements/components/<name>/<name>.js`
  (one component), `./node_modules/@raylang/elements/core.js` (the API), or
  declares an import map:
  `<script type="importmap">{ "imports": { "@raylang/elements": "./node_modules/@raylang/elements/index.js" } }</script>`.

- `npm install @raylang/elements` (React: also `@raylang/react`; Vue: also
  `@raylang/vue`). With a bundler: `import "@raylang/elements/tokens.css";`.
- Only some components: `import "@raylang/elements/button";` — one entry per
  component directory (the "Import" line of each component below). Each brings
  what it uses. `import { notify } from "@raylang/elements/notification";` gets
  a component's exports with it.
- The API without registering any element: `import { setTheme } from
  "@raylang/elements/core";`. Note that `import { RayButton } from
  "@raylang/elements"` loads everything (that entry registers every element).
- Avoid a flash of unstyled tags: `<style>:not(:defined) { visibility: hidden; }</style>`.

## Rules

- **Attributes are kebab-case, properties camelCase**: `full-width` /
  `fullWidth`. Boolean attributes are present or absent (`disabled`, never
  `disabled="false"`). Properties marked "property only" have no attribute:
  set them from JS (arrays, objects, functions). The exception is `checked`
  and `value` on form controls: their attribute is the initial state (see
  Forms).
- **Shared vocabulary**: `size` = `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl` (default
  `sm`); `radius` = `xs`…`xl` | `full`; `color` = a palette color (`blue`,
  `red`, `teal`, `gray`…) or any CSS color, default the primary; `variant` per
  component (button: `filled`, `light`, `outline`, `subtle`, `default`,
  `transparent`, `gradient`, `raised`). Use only the values the reference lists.
- **Slots have exact names**: an icon in a button goes in `slot="left"` or
  `slot="right"` (not `start`/`end`, not `prefix`): `<ray-button><ray-icon
  slot="left" name="plus"></ray-icon>Add</ray-button>`. Content without a
  `slot` goes to the default slot. Check the slot list of the component.
- **Never hard-code colors, spacing, radii or shadows** in your own CSS: use
  the tokens (`var(--ray-background)`, `var(--ray-foreground)`,
  `var(--ray-border)`, `var(--ray-space-md)`, `var(--ray-radius-default)`,
  `var(--ray-shadow-sm)`). They follow light and dark themes; literal colors do
  not. Prefer the semantic tokens over the palette (`--ray-blue-6`).
- **Style components from outside** with `color`/`variant`/`size`/`radius`,
  the tokens (custom properties pierce the shadow root) and `::part()` (the
  parts each lists). Do not reach into their
  `shadowRoot` or depend on its markup.
- **Layout components exist**: `ray-stack` (vertical), `ray-group`
  (horizontal), `ray-grid`, `ray-container`, `ray-center`, `ray-card`
  (a heading of your own in its `header` slot), `ray-app-shell`. Their
  `gap`/`padding` take `xs`…`xl`.
- **Icons**: `<ray-icon name="settings"></ray-icon>`, from the registry (a
  small set, listed in the reference: there is no `save` or `trash`); decorative unless it has `label`. An icon-only button is
  `<ray-icon-button label="Settings"><ray-icon name="settings"></ray-icon></ray-icon-button>`
  (`label` is required: it is the accessible name). Add or replace icons with
  `setIcons({ inbox: '<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round">…</svg>' })`
  (the style of the built-in set: 24×24, a 2px `currentColor` stroke) from
  your own code, never from user input. `filled` draws an icon's filled
  version for a state (`<ray-icon name="star" filled>` when it is a favorite);
  `"name:filled"` in `setIcons` adds one. An icon the set lacks (`trash`,
  `save`): register it from Lucide, the same grid and stroke —
  `import { Trash2 } from "lucide-static"; setIcons({ trash: Trash2 })` (or
  its SVG pasted in, without a bundler); never draw your own paths. To change
  one control's icon (only the chips' ×), register its role
  (`setIcons({ "ui.remove": … })`, roles listed in the reference). Under
  `dir="rtl"` the roles that point along the text (`ui.next`…) mirror by
  themselves; an icon of yours that points (back, send) takes `mirror`
  (`<ray-icon name="arrow-left" mirror>`).
- **Overlays are in the top layer**: `ray-dialog` is a native modal
  `<dialog>`; popovers, menus, tooltips and notifications are `[popover]`
  elements. Never fight them with `z-index` or `overflow`.

## An app's frame

```html
<ray-app-shell>
  <ray-app-bar slot="header" label="Files" description="No folder chosen">
    <ray-button slot="end" variant="default" size="xs">Commands</ray-button>
    <ray-theme-toggle slot="end"></ray-theme-toggle>
  </ray-app-bar>
  <ray-sidebar slot="navbar" label="Workspace">
    <ray-nav-link label="Files" href="#files" active><ray-icon slot="left" name="folder"></ray-icon></ray-nav-link>
    <ray-nav-link label="Settings" href="#settings"><ray-icon slot="left" name="settings"></ray-icon></ray-nav-link>
  </ray-sidebar>
  <main>…</main>
</ray-app-shell>
```

`ray-app-bar` is the header on the desktop too (its `label` is the title;
several elements may share the `end` slot). On narrow screens the sidebar
becomes a drawer and the shell switches to a phone layout by itself.

## Forms

- Inputs are **form-associated**: inside a `<form>` they submit under `name`,
  validate (`required`, `pattern`, `min`…), reset with it and follow a
  disabled `<fieldset>`. Read values with `new FormData(form)` or the
  element's `.value` / `.checked`.
- The `value` / `checked` **attributes are the initial value**; the
  properties hold the current one. Set `el.value = …` to change it.
- Fields take `label`, `description` and `error` (the error text also marks it
  invalid): do not wrap them in your own `<label>`.
- Enter in a `ray-input` submits its form, as in a native field; a submit
  button is `<ray-button type="submit">`.
- As with native controls: an invalid field (`required` and empty, a wrong
  `type="email"`…) blocks the submit and the browser shows its message; an
  unchecked `ray-checkbox`/`ray-switch` and a `ray-select` with nothing chosen
  are left out of `FormData` (a select's `placeholder` shows meanwhile).

## Events

- A value change is a plain `input` (while typing) and `change` event: read
  `event.target.value`.
- Everything else is a `ray-*` custom event (bubbles, composed) with its data
  in `event.detail`: `ray-select` on a menu (`detail.value`), `ray-close` on a
  dialog (`detail.returnValue`), `ray-request-close` (cancelable). The
  reference lists each component's events and their `detail`.

## Dialogs and notifications

```html
<ray-dialog id="d" label="Rename">
  <ray-input label="Name" name="name"></ray-input>
  <ray-button slot="footer" variant="default" data-dialog-close>Cancel</ray-button>
  <ray-button slot="footer" data-dialog-close="ok">Save</ray-button>
</ray-dialog>
```

`d.show()` or the `open` attribute opens it; any slotted element with
`data-dialog-close` closes it (its value becomes `returnValue`); the close
button, Escape and the backdrop close it with `returnValue` `""` (after a
cancelable `ray-request-close`).
`await confirmDialog({ label, message, confirmLabel, cancelLabel, color: "red" })`
asks a yes/no question (every option is optional: "Are you sure?",
"Confirm", "Cancel"); `notify({ title, message, color })` shows a
notification (`message` is plain text; a `color` adds a status icon:
green a check, red an error, yellow a warning, others info).

## Theme

- The theme follows the system. Force it on the page or any subtree with
  `data-theme="light"` | `"dark"`; change the primary color with
  `data-primary="violet"` (a palette color).
- From JS: `setTheme("light" | "dark" | "system")`, `setPrimary("violet")`,
  `definePrimary("#7c3aed")` (any brand color: builds the ten shades and
  checks contrast), `onThemeChange(cb)`. `<ray-theme-toggle>` is the switch.
- App-wide defaults for a component: `configure({ defaults: { "ray-button":
  { variant: "light" } } })`.

## Right to left

- `dir="rtl"` on `<html>` (with its `lang`) or a subtree mirrors the
  components: layout, the icons that point along the text, arrow keys
  (ArrowLeft is forward), sliders, carousels, splits and floating panels
  (`bottom-start` lines up with the right edge). Nothing to configure.
- For a side, write `start`/`end` (they follow the direction):
  `label-position="start"`, `<ray-drawer position="start">`,
  `<ray-sidebar side="end">`, `<ray-toaster position="top-start">`.
  `left`/`right` are sides of the screen whatever the direction; use them
  only when the side is meant (a map's legend).
- Your own CSS: logical properties (`margin-inline-start`, `inset-inline-end`,
  `text-align: start`), never `left`/`right`; an icon of yours that points
  (back, send) takes `mirror`.

## React and Vue

```tsx
import "@raylang/elements/tokens.css";
import { RayInput, RayMenu, RayMenuItem, RayButton } from "@raylang/react";

<RayInput label="Name" value={name} onInput={(e) => setName(e.currentTarget.value)} />
<RayMenu onRaySelect={(e) => run(e.detail.value)}>
  <RayButton slot="trigger">Actions</RayButton>
  <RayMenuItem value="rename">Rename</RayMenuItem>
</RayMenu>
```

```vue
<!-- main.ts: import RayElements from "@raylang/vue"; app.use(RayElements) -->
<RayInput v-model="name" label="Name" required />
<RayDialog v-model="open" label="Confirm" @ray-close="onClose">…</RayDialog>
```

- The wrapper of `<ray-tag-name>` is `RayTagName`. React events are `on` +
  PascalCase of the event (`onRaySelect`, `onChange`); props are set as DOM
  properties. Vue has `v-model` where the reference lists a model (`value`,
  `checked` or `open`).
- A wrapper registers only its own element: a plain `<ray-*>` tag in JSX
  needs its import (`import "@raylang/elements/badge"`).

## In a raylang app

`ray add elements` brings the raylang package `elements`: it serves
`@raylang/elements` to the app's pages by its npm name, with no npm and no
build step. The page:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/node_modules/@raylang/elements/tokens.css">
<script type="module">
  import { enableRaylang } from "@raylang/elements";
  const host = await enableRaylang();   // the native host, or null in a browser
</script>
```

The program serves the page and answers the bridge before its own events:

```ray
import std/ui;
import elements/bridge;

fn main() -> int {
    match (run()) {
        Result.Ok(code) => code,
        Result.Err(e) => {
            eprint(e);
            1
        },
    }
}

fn run() -> Result<int, string> {
    ui.mount_embed_at("", "assets")?;   // the page: assets/index.html, ray.toml [native] embed = ["assets"]
    ui.open_with("App", "ray://app/index.html", ui.options(800, 600))?;
    while (true) {
        let e = ui.next_event()?;
        if (bridge.handle(e)) {
            continue;   // a ray-elements request, already answered
        }
        if (e.kind == "closed") {
            return Result.Ok(0);
        }
        // the app's own events: e.kind == "message" (window.ray.send), e.tag…
    }
}
```

With the bridge: `<ray-file-upload native>` and `<ray-path-input>` use the
system file dialogs and give real paths, `confirmDialog()` asks with the
system dialog, `<ray-menu native>` opens a native context menu,
`<ray-command-palette native-menus>` runs the app's menu bar
(`bridge.menu`, `bridge.route`), `ray-app-shell` becomes the title bar of a
`full_content` window, and `trackEdits(form)` shows the unsaved mark. The
components that use it have an "In a raylang app" section. Without the
bridge every component keeps its web behavior.

## Check your markup

The package checks markup against this version:
`npx ray-elements check src/` (with npm), or
`node node_modules/@raylang/elements/check/cli.js check assets/` (a raylang
app). It reports unknown elements, attributes, slots and `ray-*` events,
invalid values, unregistered icons and literal colors, with the line and a
suggestion, and exits with 1 on an error. Run it after writing a page and fix
what it reports; `--format json` gives the diagnostics as JSON.

## Your own components

Extend `RayElement`, `FormControl`, `FieldControl` or `Floating` (or any
component class) from `@raylang/elements/core`; see the Extending guide.
Members whose name starts with `_` are internal.

## Components

### Base classes

Properties the components inherit from the base classes (each component lists which it extends):

FieldControl (extends FormControl):

- `name`: string. Form field name.
- `label`: string. Visible label (also the accessible name).
- `description`: string. Help text.
- `error`: string. Error text; marks the field invalid.
- `required`: boolean, reflects. Required for form submission.
- `disabled`: boolean, reflects. Not interactive nor submitted.
- `size`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`, default `sm`, reflects. Size.
- `radius`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl` | `full`, reflects. Corner radius.
- `variant`: `default` | `filled` | `unstyled`, default `default`, reflects. Box style.
- `descriptionPosition` (attribute `description-position`): `above` | `below`, default `above`, reflects. Description before or after the control.

Floating (extends RayElement):

- `open`: boolean, reflects. Shown.
- `placement`: string, default `bottom`, reflects. Preferred side and alignment.
- `offset`: number, default `8`. Gap to the anchor in px.

### Button

A button, or a link styled as one with href. Submits or resets its form with type.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/button";` · Category: Buttons

#### `<ray-button>` (RayButton, extends RayElement)

Properties:

- `variant`: `filled` | `light` | `outline` | `subtle` | `default` | `transparent` | `gradient` | `raised`, default `filled`, reflects. Visual style. raised: a physical key on a darker edge that sinks when pressed (mouse, touch or keyboard).
- `gradient`: string, reflects. With variant=gradient: "from to [deg]", palette colors or CSS colors ("teal blue 90"). Default: the --ray-gradient-* tokens.
- `color`: string. A palette color (blue, red…) or any CSS color. Default: the primary color.
- `size`: `"xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | (string & {})`, default `sm`, reflects. Height, padding and font size: xs…xl or any CSS length (the padding and the font follow).
- `radius`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl` | `full`. Corner radius. Default: --ray-radius-default.
- `type`: `button` | `submit` | `reset`, default `button`. submit/reset act on the enclosing form.
- `disabled`: boolean. Not interactive (also when inside a disabled fieldset).
- `loading`: boolean. Shows a spinner over the content and blocks clicks.
- `fullWidth` (attribute `full-width`): boolean. Takes the whole width of its container.
- `href`: string. Renders a link instead of a button.
- `target`: string. Link target, with href.
- `name`: string. With type=submit: submitted as name=value.
- `value`: string. With type=submit: the submitted value.

Slots:

- (default): The label.
- `left`: Icon or content before the label.
- `right`: Icon or content after the label.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `button`: The inner <button> or <a>.
- `label`: The label wrapper.

Methods and properties:

- `readonly form: HTMLFormElement | null`: The form a submit/reset button acts on.

### Button group

Buttons joined into one control: inner corners squared, borders overlapped. Works with ray-button, ray-icon-button, menus with a button trigger and fields (ray-input, ray-select, ray-search).

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/button-group";` · Category: Buttons

#### `<ray-button-group>` (RayButtonGroup, extends RayElement)

role=group; give it a label. The corners come from the --ray-group-radius-* custom properties, which your own components can read too.

Properties:

- `orientation`: `horizontal` | `vertical`, default `horizontal`, reflects. Direction of the group.
- `fullWidth` (attribute `full-width`): boolean, reflects. Fills its container; the children share the width.
- `label`: string. Accessible name (aria-label).

Slots:

- (default): The buttons, fields or menus to join.

### Icon button

A square button for an icon (Mantine's ActionIcon). Always give it a label.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/icon-button";` · Category: Buttons

#### `<ray-icon-button>` (RayIconButton, extends RayButton)

Same properties as ray-button; variant defaults to subtle.

Properties:

- `label`: string, reflects. Accessible name and tooltip (required: the button has no text).
- `variant`: `filled` | `light` | `outline` | `subtle` | `default` | `transparent` | `gradient` | `raised`, default `subtle`, reflects. Visual style.
- `gradient`: string, reflects. With variant=gradient: "from to [deg]", palette colors or CSS colors ("teal blue 90"). Default: the --ray-gradient-* tokens.
- `color`: string. A palette color or any CSS color.
- `size`: `"xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | (string & {})`, default `sm`, reflects. Width and height: xs…xl or any CSS length ("5.5rem": a big main action, round with radius=full); the icon scales with it.
- `disabled`: boolean. Not interactive.
- `loading`: boolean. Shows a spinner instead of the icon.

Also the properties of RayButton (`<ray-button>`): `radius`, `type`, `fullWidth`, `href`, `target`, `name`, `value`.

Slots:

- (default): The icon (an inline <svg> is sized to the button).

Parts (`::part()`):

- `button`: The inner button.

### Toggle

A two-state button (aria-pressed): bold in a toolbar, mute, favorite. The variant is how "on" looks; "off" is always neutral, so the states differ by more than color. Has everything ray-button has and joins a ray-button-group.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/toggle";` · Category: Buttons

#### `<ray-toggle>` (RayToggle, extends RayButton)

Click, Enter or Space flips pressed and fires change. In a form it is submitted like a checkbox: value (default "on") under name while pressed; reset restores the initial pressed attribute.

Properties:

- `pressed`: boolean, reflects. On.
- `variant`: `subtle` | `outline` | `light` | `filled` | `raised`, default `subtle`, reflects. Look of "on": subtle (tint), outline (colored border + tint), light (muted → tint), filled (surface → solid color), raised (a key that latches down, lit). ray-button's default, transparent and gradient are left out: no distinct on state, or only a color change.
- `square`: boolean, reflects. Square, for an icon alone (give it a label).
- `label`: string, reflects. Accessible name and tooltip, for icon-only toggles.

Also the properties of RayButton (`<ray-button>`): `gradient`, `color`, `size`, `radius`, `type`, `disabled`, `loading`, `fullWidth`, `href`, `target`, `name`, `value`.

Events:

- `change`: The user flipped it (read `pressed`).

Slots:

- (default): Text or an icon.

### Toggle group

ray-toggle elements with one shared value: type="single" (at most one on: alignment, view mode) or "multiple" (bold / italic / underline). Joined like a button group, or spaced; arrow keys move between toggles; submitted with its form.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/toggle-group";` · Category: Buttons

#### `<ray-toggle-group>` (RayToggleGroup, extends RayButtonGroup)

Each toggle's value (else its text) is its key. variant, color, size, radius and square reach the toggles that do not set their own. One tab stop (the selected toggle); arrows, Home and End move; Space/Enter flips.

Properties:

- `type`: `single` | `multiple`, default `single`, reflects. single: choosing one turns the others off; multiple: each toggle is independent.
- `value`: `string | string[] | undefined`. The selected key (single) or keys (multiple: an array, or a comma-separated attribute).
- `name`: string, reflects. Form field name: the value (multiple: one entry per key).
- `required`: boolean, reflects. Needs a value; with single the selected toggle cannot be turned off.
- `disabled`: boolean, reflects. Disables every toggle.
- `spaced`: boolean, reflects. Toggles apart, each with its own corners (default: joined).
- `variant`: `subtle` | `outline` | `light` | `filled` | `raised`, reflects. Variant of the toggles.
- `color`: string, reflects. Color of the toggles' on state.
- `size`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`, reflects. Size of the toggles.
- `radius`: string, reflects. Corner radius of the toggles.
- `square`: boolean, reflects. Square toggles, for icons.

Also the properties of RayButtonGroup (`<ray-button-group>`): `orientation`, `fullWidth`, `label`.

Events:

- `change`: The user changed the selection (read `value` or `values`; the toggles' own change events stop at the group).

Slots:

- (default): ray-toggle elements.

Methods and properties:

- `values: string[]`: The selected keys as a list, in any mode.
- `readonly toggles: RayToggle[]`: The toggles of this group.

### Checkbox

A checkbox with label, description and error. Submits value when checked.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/checkbox";` · Category: Inputs

#### `<ray-checkbox>` (RayCheckbox, extends FieldControl)

Properties:

- `checked` (attribute `checked`: the initial value only): boolean. Current state. The checked attribute is the initial state (restored on reset).
- `indeterminate`: boolean, reflects. Mixed state; cleared on the next user change.
- `value`: string, default `on`, reflects. Submitted value when checked.
- `name`: string. Form field name.
- `label`: string. Label text (or put the label in the content).
- `description`: string. Help text.
- `error`: string. Error text.
- `required`: boolean. Must be checked to submit.
- `disabled`: boolean. Not interactive nor submitted.
- `variant`: `filled` | `outline`, default `filled`, reflects. Checked look: filled box, or colored border and mark.
- `color`: string. A palette color or any CSS color for the checked state.
- `size`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`, default `sm`, reflects. Box and font size.
- `labelPosition` (attribute `label-position`): `end` | `start` | `right` | `left`, default `end`, reflects. Side of the label: start/end follow the writing direction; left/right are sides of the screen.

Also the properties of FieldControl: `radius`, `descriptionPosition`.

Events:

- `change`: When the user toggles it.

Slots:

- (default): Label content.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `input`: The native checkbox (transparent, on top of the indicator).
- `indicator`: The drawn box.
- `label`: The label.

Vue `v-model`: `checked` (updated on change).

### Checkbox group

Several choices among options (Mantine's Checkbox.Group): a label, description and error around ray-checkbox elements; the value is the array of the checked ones. max caps how many; required asks for one.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/checkbox-group";` · Category: Inputs

#### `<ray-checkbox-group>` (RayCheckboxGroup, extends FormControl)

The group is the form control: one entry per checked value under name (like checkboxes sharing a name); the checkboxes inside lose their own name. It stops their change events and fires its own. role="group" named by its label.

Properties:

- `value` (attribute `value`: the initial value only): `string[]`. The checked values. The value attribute: "a,b".
- `name`: string, reflects. Form field name.
- `label`: string. Group label (also its accessible name).
- `description`: string. Help text.
- `error`: string. Error text.
- `required`: boolean, reflects. At least one must be checked.
- `disabled`: boolean, reflects. Disables every checkbox.
- `max`: number. At most this many: the others are disabled once reached; the label shows the count.
- `orientation`: `vertical` | `horizontal`, default `vertical`, reflects. Layout of the checkboxes.
- `size`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`, reflects. Size of the checkboxes that set none.
- `color`: string, reflects. Color of the checkboxes that set none.
- `descriptionPosition` (attribute `description-position`): `above` | `below`, default `above`, reflects. The description before the checkboxes or after them.

Events:

- `change`: The user checked or unchecked one (read value).
- `input`: Same moment as change.

Slots:

- (default): ray-checkbox elements (also nested in other markup).

Methods and properties:

- `readonly checkboxes: HTMLElement[]`: The checkboxes of this group.

Vue `v-model`: `value` (updated on change).

### Color picker

Pick a color: an inline picker (saturation area, hue, opacity, swatches) and a text field with the picker in a dropdown and an eyedropper. Pointer and keyboard; form-associated; hex, rgb or hsl, with or without alpha.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/color-picker";` · Category: Inputs

#### `<ray-color-picker>` (RayColorPicker, extends FormControl)

Keyboard: arrows move the area's thumb (saturation, brightness) or a slider's; Shift for 10× steps; Home/End on the sliders. The alpha slider shows when format has alpha.

Properties:

- `value`: string. The color, written in format. Any color is accepted and rewritten in format. The value attribute is the initial value (restored on form reset).
- `format`: `ColorFormat`, default `hex`, reflects. How value is written: hex, hexa, rgb, rgba, hsl or hsla. Formats ending in a show the opacity slider.
- `swatches`: `string | string[]`. Preset colors below the picker: an array, or a comma-separated list in the attribute (commas inside rgb()/hsl() are kept).
- `swatchesPerRow` (attribute `swatches-per-row`): number, default `7`. Swatches in each row.
- `swatchesOnly` (attribute `swatches-only`): boolean, reflects. Only the swatches: no area nor sliders.
- `size`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`, default `md`, reflects. Width of the picker and size of its thumbs.
- `fullWidth` (attribute `full-width`): boolean, reflects. Takes the width of its container.
- `name`: string, reflects. Form field name.
- `disabled`: boolean, reflects. Not interactive.
- `label`: string. Accessible name of the whole picker.

Events:

- `input`: The color moved (every step of a drag).
- `change`: The color settled: pointer released, a key pressed or a swatch chosen (read value).

Parts (`::part()`):

- `saturation`: The saturation/brightness area.
- `hue`: The hue slider.
- `alpha`: The opacity slider.
- `preview`: The current color.
- `swatches`: The swatches' grid.

Methods and properties:

- `readonly rgba: Rgba`: The current color as channels and alpha (0…1).

Vue `v-model`: `value` (updated on input).

#### `<ray-color-input>` (RayColorInput, extends FieldControl)

Type any CSS color (it becomes the value as soon as it is valid; invalid text goes back to the value on blur), or open the picker with a click or ArrowDown. The eyedropper shows only where the browser has the EyeDropper API.

Properties:

- `value`: string. The color, written in format. The value attribute is the initial value (restored on form reset).
- `format`: `ColorFormat`, default `hex`, reflects. How value is written: hex, hexa, rgb, rgba, hsl or hsla.
- `swatches`: `string | string[]`. Preset colors in the dropdown (an array, or a comma-separated list).
- `swatchesPerRow` (attribute `swatches-per-row`): number, default `7`. Swatches in each row.
- `placeholder`: string. Shown while empty.
- `hideEyedropper` (attribute `hide-eyedropper`): boolean, reflects. Hides the eyedropper button.
- `open`: boolean, reflects. The dropdown is shown.
- `name`: string, reflects. Form field name.
- `label`: string. Label above the field.
- `description`: string. Help text.
- `error`: string. Error message; marks the field invalid.
- `required`: boolean, reflects. Must have a color.
- `disabled`: boolean, reflects. Not interactive.
- `size`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`, default `sm`, reflects. Field height and font size.
- `radius`: string, reflects. Corner radius: xs…xl or a CSS length.
- `variant`: `default` | `filled` | `unstyled`, default `default`, reflects. Visual style of the field.
- `descriptionPosition` (attribute `description-position`): `above` | `below`, default `above`, reflects. Where the description goes.

Events:

- `input`: The color changed (typing a valid color, or moving the picker).
- `change`: The color settled (picker released, a swatch, the eyedropper, or the field left with a new color).
- `ray-open`: The dropdown opened.
- `ray-close`: The dropdown closed.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `input`: The text field.
- `preview`: The swatch of the current color.
- `eyedropper`: The eyedropper button.
- `dropdown`: The dropdown with the picker.

Methods and properties:

- `readonly picker: RayColorPicker`: The ray-color-picker in the dropdown.
- `toggle(force?: boolean): void`: Opens or closes the dropdown.

Vue `v-model`: `value` (updated on input).

Exports (from `@raylang/elements/color-picker` and `@raylang/elements`):

- `function parseColorValue(input: string | null | undefined): Rgba | null`: A color string (hex with 3/4/6/8 digits, rgb(a), hsl(a), or any CSS color) as channels and alpha, or null.
- `function formatColor(color: Rgba, format?: ColorFormat): string`: Channels and alpha as a string in a format (default hex).

Types:

- `"hex" | "hexa" | "rgb" | "rgba" | "hsl" | "hsla"`: How a color value is written.
- `{ r: number; g: number; b: number; a: number }`: sRGB channels and alpha, all 0…1.

### Combobox (also Multi select)

A select you can type in, an autocomplete (Mantine's searchable Select, MultiSelect and TagsInput): typing filters the options; multiple keeps chips; creatable adds new values; clearable, max-values, groups, a result limit.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/combobox";` · Category: Inputs

#### `<ray-combobox>` (RayCombobox, extends FieldControl)

The WAI-ARIA combobox pattern (a text field with a listbox popup; the active option is aria-activedescendant). Arrows move, Enter picks, Escape closes (then clears with clearable), Backspace in an empty field removes the last chip. The form gets one entry per value.

Properties:

- `value` (attribute `value`: the initial value only): `string | string[]`. The chosen value; an array with multiple. The value attribute: "a,b" with multiple.
- `data` (property only): `Array<string | { value: string; label?: string; disabled?: boolean; group?: string }>`. Options instead of child <option>/<optgroup> elements.
- `multiple`: boolean, reflects. Several values, shown as chips.
- `placeholder`: string. Shown while empty.
- `creatable`: boolean. What was typed can be added when no option matches it ("+ Create …"); fires ray-create.
- `clearable`: boolean. A button that clears the value.
- `maxValues` (attribute `max-values`): number. With multiple: at most this many.
- `limit`: number. At most this many options shown (large lists: keep typing).
- `nothingFound` (attribute `nothing-found`): string, default `No matches`. Shown when nothing matches.
- `open`: boolean, reflects. The dropdown is shown.

Also the properties of FieldControl: `name`, `label`, `description`, `error`, `required`, `disabled`, `size`, `radius`, `variant`, `descriptionPosition`.

Events:

- `change`: The value changed (read value).
- `input`: Same moment as change.
- `ray-create` (detail `{ value: string }`): A new value was created from the typed text.
- `ray-open`: The dropdown opened.
- `ray-close`: The dropdown closed.

Slots:

- (default): <option> and <optgroup> elements.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `input`: The text field.
- `chips`: The chips container.
- `chip`: A chip.
- `clear`: The clear button.
- `dropdown`: The listbox.
- `option`: An option.

Methods and properties:

- `readonly values: string[]`: The value as an array (with or without multiple).
- `toggle(force?: boolean): void`: Opens or closes the dropdown.

Vue `v-model`: `value` (updated on change).

### Date picker

A date field with a calendar dropdown, and the calendar on its own. Keyboard grid navigation, min/max, locale-aware. Form-associated.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/date-picker";` · Category: Inputs

#### `<ray-date-picker>` (RayDatePicker, extends FieldControl)

Values are ISO dates ("2026-10-06"), submitted as such. ArrowDown on the field opens the calendar; Escape closes it.

Properties:

- `value`: string. The chosen date, ISO "YYYY-MM-DD" ("" for none). The value attribute is the initial value (restored on form reset).
- `min`: string. Earliest selectable date (ISO). Earlier days are disabled; an earlier value is invalid (rangeUnderflow).
- `max`: string. Latest selectable date (ISO).
- `placeholder`: string, default `Pick a date`. Shown while no date is chosen.
- `format`: `short` | `medium` | `long` | `full`, default `medium`. How the date is displayed (Intl dateStyle).
- `locale`: string. Locale for names and formats. Default: the nearest lang attribute, else the browser's.
- `firstDay` (attribute `first-day`): number. First day of the week, 0 (Sunday) to 6. Default: the locale's.
- `clearable`: boolean, reflects. Shows a button that clears the date.
- `open`: boolean, reflects. The calendar dropdown is shown.
- `name`: string, reflects. Form field name.
- `label`: string. Visible label (also the accessible name).
- `description`: string. Help text.
- `descriptionPosition` (attribute `description-position`): `above` | `below`, default `above`, reflects. The description before the control (help first) or after it, with the error (fields in a row stay aligned).
- `error`: string. Error text.
- `required`: boolean. Required for form submission.
- `disabled`: boolean. Not interactive nor submitted.
- `size`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`, default `sm`, reflects. Height and font size.
- `radius`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl` | `full`. Corner radius.
- `variant`: `default` | `filled` | `unstyled`, default `default`, reflects. Box style.

Events:

- `input`: When the date changes (picked or cleared).
- `change`: When the date changes (picked or cleared).
- `ray-open`: The calendar opened.
- `ray-close`: The calendar closed.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `trigger`: The button showing the date.
- `clear`: The clear button.
- `dropdown`: The calendar panel (a popover in the top layer).
- `calendar`: The <ray-calendar> in the dropdown (its day, caption, nav and grid parts are exported).
- `input`: The hidden native <input type=date> that holds the value (the model).
- `wrapper`: The box.

Methods and properties:

- `toggle(force?: boolean): void`: Opens or closes the calendar.
- `readonly displayValue: string`: The chosen date as displayed ("" when none).

Vue `v-model`: `value` (updated on change).

#### `<ray-calendar>` (RayCalendar, extends RayElement)

WAI-ARIA grid: arrows move by day and week, Home/End to the week's ends, PageUp/PageDown by month (with Shift, by year), Enter/Space select.

Properties:

- `value`: string. The selected date, ISO "YYYY-MM-DD".
- `min`: string. Earliest selectable date (ISO).
- `max`: string. Latest selectable date (ISO).
- `locale`: string. Locale for month and weekday names. Default: the nearest lang attribute, else the browser's.
- `firstDay` (attribute `first-day`): number. First day of the week, 0 (Sunday) to 6. Default: the locale's.
- `size`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`, default `sm`, reflects. Day cell size and font size.

Events:

- `change`: A day was selected (read `value`).

Parts (`::part()`):

- `header`: The row with the month and the navigation buttons.
- `caption`: The month and year.
- `nav`: The previous/next month buttons.
- `grid`: The day grid (role=grid).
- `day`: Each day button ([aria-selected], [aria-current=date], [aria-disabled], [data-outside]).

Methods and properties:

- `focusDay(): void`: Focuses the day the keyboard is on (the selected day, else today).
- `readonly focusedDate: string`: The day the keyboard is on (ISO).

Vue `v-model`: `value` (updated on change).

### File upload

A drop zone to pick files: drag, click, keyboard or paste. Checks type, size and count as files arrive, lists them as ray-attachment rows (thumbnails, remove) and submits them with its form.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/file-upload";` · Category: Inputs

#### `<ray-file-upload>` (RayFileUpload, extends FormControl)

A drag that can only be refused turns the zone red before the drop; refused files fire ray-reject and are explained under the zone. Without multiple a new file replaces the current one. Uploading is the app's: attachmentFor(file) gives the row whose progress/status/error to set.

Properties:

- `name`: string, reflects. Form field name: every file is submitted under it.
- `label`: string. Label above the zone.
- `description`: string. Help text under the label.
- `error`: string. Error text (replaces the explanation of refused files).
- `required`: boolean, reflects. The form needs at least one file.
- `disabled`: boolean, reflects. No picking, dropping or removing.
- `accept`: string, reflects. Accepted types, as in <input type=file>: ".pdf,.png", "image/*", "application/json".
- `multiple`: boolean, reflects. Several files (else one, replaced by the next).
- `maxSize` (attribute `max-size`): `string | number`. Largest file: bytes or a size like "10 MB", "512 KB".
- `maxFiles` (attribute `max-files`): number. With multiple: the most files kept.
- `hint`: string. Small text in the zone. Default: from accept, max-size and max-files ("PNG or PDF · up to 10 MB each · max. 5 files").
- `dropLabel` (attribute `drop-label`): string, default `Drag files here`. Title of the zone, before "or browse".
- `browseLabel` (attribute `browse-label`): string, default `browse`. The link-styled word (the button text in compact).
- `activeLabel` (attribute `active-label`): string, default `Drop to add files`. Title while files are dragged over it.
- `tapLabel` (attribute `tap-label`): string, default `Choose files`. Title on touch screens (no hover), where dragging files is rare.
- `variant`: `default` | `compact`, default `default`, reflects. default: a tall centered zone; compact: one row with a Browse button.
- `list`: `rows` | `cards` | `none`, default `rows`, reflects. How chosen files show: full-width rows, thumbnail cards, or not at all (render your own on change).
- `native`: boolean, reflects. With a native host (ray-elements/core/raylang.js in a std/ui window), browsing opens the system dialog and gives paths (see `paths`); drop and paste still give Files.
- `color`: string, reflects. Accent of hover, drag and the browse link (default: primary).

Events:

- `change`: Files were added or removed (read `files`, and `lastChange` for which).
- `ray-reject` (detail `{ rejected: FileRejection[] }`): Some files were refused (type, size or count).
- `ray-error` (detail `{ error: Error }`): The native dialog failed (with `native`).

Slots:

- `icon`: Replaces the upload icon.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `dropzone`: The zone (a button).
- `icon`: The icon tile.
- `hint`: The small text in the zone.
- `files`: The list of chosen files.
- `label`: The label.
- `error`: The error text.

Methods and properties:

- `files: (File | HostFile)[]`: The chosen files (assign to replace them, without events).
- `readonly paths: string[]`: The paths of the files chosen with the native dialog (`native`), in order; they are also what the form submits for them.
- `readonly lastChange: FileUploadChange | null`: What the last change event changed: the files added and removed. null before the first one, and after assigning files.
- `open(): void`: Opens the system file picker.
- `addFiles(files: Iterable<File>): { accepted: File[]; rejected: FileRejection[] }`: Adds files as if dropped (checks them, fires the events).
- `removeFile(file: File): boolean`: Removes a file (fires change).
- `clear(): void`: Removes every file (fires change).
- `attachmentFor(file: File): RayAttachment | null`: The row of a file, to show its upload progress, status or error.

Exports (from `@raylang/elements/file-upload` and `@raylang/elements`):

- `function parseSize(value: string | number | null | undefined): number`: Bytes from a number or a size like "10 MB" (NaN if neither).
- `function matchesAccept(file: { name: string; type: string }, accept: string | null | undefined): boolean`: Whether a file passes an accept list.
- `function describeAccept(accept: string | null | undefined): string`: A short human list of an accept value ("PNG, JPG or PDF").

Types:

- `{ added: (File | HostFile)[]; removed: (File | HostFile)[] }`: The files a change added and removed.
- `{ file: File; reason: "type" | "size" | "count"; message: string }`: A refused file and why.

#### In a raylang app

In a `std/ui` window with [the native bridge](https://elements.raylang.dev/raylang.html#using-the-bridge), `native` makes browsing open the system's file dialog, with the `accept` types as its filter. The files it gives are paths on the user's disk, not bytes: they list like any other file (name, size, type) and the program reads them.

```html
<form id="import">
  <ray-file-upload name="photos" native multiple accept="image/*" label="Photos"></ray-file-upload>
</form>
```

```js
upload.addEventListener("change", () => {
  window.ray.send("import:" + JSON.stringify(upload.paths));   // ["/Users/ada/Pictures/a.jpg", …]
});
```

The form submits those paths under `name`. Dropped and pasted files are still `File` objects (`upload.files` holds both; a chosen one is a `HostFile` with a `path`). Without the bridge, or in a browser, `native` changes nothing.

### Input

A text field with label, description and error (Mantine's TextInput). Form-associated.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/input";` · Category: Inputs

#### `<ray-input>` (RayInput, extends FieldControl)

Also forwards placeholder, autocomplete, inputmode, pattern, min, max, step, minlength, maxlength, spellcheck, autocapitalize, enterkeyhint and list to the inner input. Enter submits its form as a native field does: through the first submit button (ray-button type="submit" included; nothing when it is disabled), or, without one, only when the form has a single text field.

Properties:

- `value`: string. Current value. The value attribute is the initial value (restored on form reset).
- `type`: `text` | `email` | `password` | `search` | `number` | `url` | `tel`, default `text`, reflects. Input type.
- `name`: string, reflects. Form field name.
- `label`: string. Visible label (also the accessible name).
- `description`: string. Help text under the label.
- `descriptionPosition` (attribute `description-position`): `above` | `below`, default `above`, reflects. The description before the control (help first) or after it, with the error (fields in a row stay aligned).
- `error`: string. Error text; marks the field invalid (display only — does not block submit).
- `placeholder`: string. Placeholder text.
- `required`: boolean. Required for form submission; shows an asterisk.
- `disabled`: boolean. Not editable nor submitted.
- `readonly`: boolean. Not editable, still submitted.
- `size`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`, default `sm`, reflects. Height and font size.
- `radius`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl` | `full`. Corner radius.
- `variant`: `default` | `filled` | `unstyled`, default `default`, reflects. Box style.

Attributes (forwarded to the inner element):

- `autocomplete`: Forwarded to the inner input.
- `inputmode`: Virtual keyboard hint.
- `pattern`: Validation pattern (regular expression).
- `min`: Minimum (number/date types).
- `max`: Maximum (number/date types).
- `step`: Step (number types).
- `minlength`: Minimum length.
- `maxlength`: Maximum length.
- `autocapitalize`: Mobile auto-capitalization.
- `enterkeyhint`: Label of the Enter key on virtual keyboards.
- `list`: Id of a <datalist> with suggestions.

Events:

- `input`: On every edit (value already updated).
- `change`: When an edit is committed (blur, Enter).

Slots:

- `left`: Section before the text (icon).
- `right`: Section after the text (icon, button).

Parts (`::part()`):

- `input`: The inner <input>.
- `wrapper`: The box around the input and sections.
- `label`: The label.
- `description`: The description.
- `error`: The error message.

Methods and properties:

- `select(): void`: Selects the text.

Vue `v-model`: `value` (updated on input).

### Number input

A number field (Mantine's NumberInput): + and − buttons (hold to repeat), arrow keys, min, max and step, fixed decimals, a prefix and a suffix, a thousands separator, or a duration (m:ss). An ARIA spinbutton.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/number-input";` · Category: Inputs

#### `<ray-number-input>` (RayNumberInput, extends FieldControl)

Arrow Up/Down step (Shift: ×10), Page Up/Down ×10, Home/End go to min/max. The value is a number (undefined when empty); the form gets its plain digits; min and max are checked (rangeUnderflow, rangeOverflow). Enter submits its form, as in ray-input.

Properties:

- `value`: number. The number (undefined when empty).
- `min`: number. Minimum.
- `max`: number. Maximum.
- `step`: number, default `1`. What + and − add.
- `decimals`: number. Fixed decimals (2: 3 shows as 3.00).
- `prefix`: `string | null`. Shown before the number ("$").
- `suffix`: string. Shown after the number (" kg", "%").
- `thousandsSeparator` (attribute `thousands-separator`): string. Groups thousands in the shown text (",", ".", " ").
- `decimalSeparator` (attribute `decimal-separator`): string, default `.`. The decimal mark shown and typed ("," in many locales).
- `clamp`: `blur` | `strict` | `none`, default `blur`. When out-of-range input is clamped: on blur, while typing, or never (then it is invalid).
- `format`: `number` | `duration`, default `number`, reflects. duration: the value is seconds, shown and typed as m:ss (h:mm:ss when min or max reaches an hour; a plain number is seconds); aria-valuetext says "3 minutes, 15 seconds" in the page's language. decimals, prefix, suffix and the separators do not apply.
- `hideControls` (attribute `hide-controls`): boolean, reflects. No + and − buttons (the keys still step).
- `placeholder`: string. Shown while empty.
- `readonly`: boolean, reflects. Not editable, still submitted.

Also the properties of FieldControl: `name`, `label`, `description`, `error`, `required`, `disabled`, `size`, `radius`, `variant`, `descriptionPosition`.

Events:

- `input`: On every change of the value (typing, keys, buttons).
- `change`: When the value is committed (blur, a step).

Slots:

- `left`: Left section (an icon).
- `right`: Right section.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `input`: The text field.
- `controls`: The + and − column.
- `increment`: The + button.
- `decrement`: The − button.

Methods and properties:

- `stepBy(steps: number): void`: Adds steps (negative: subtracts), clamped; fires input and change.

Vue `v-model`: `value` (updated on input).

Exports (from `@raylang/elements/number-input` and `@raylang/elements`):

- `function parseNumber(text: string, options?: { decimal?: string; thousands?: string }): number`: The number in a text with separators, prefix or suffix (NaN if none).
- `function formatNumber(n: number, options?: { decimals?: number; thousands?: string; decimal?: string }): string`: A number as text with fixed decimals and separators.

### Password input

A password field with a button that shows or hides what was typed (Mantine's PasswordInput). Everything else is ray-input: label, description, error, sizes, validation, forms.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/password-input";` · Category: Inputs

#### `<ray-password-input>` (RayPasswordInput, extends RayInput)

autocomplete defaults to current-password: use new-password on sign-up and change forms. The toggle keeps the focus and the caret in the field.

Properties:

- `visible`: boolean, reflects. The password is shown as text.
- `showLabel` (attribute `show-label`): string, default `Show password`. Accessible name of the toggle while hidden.
- `hideLabel` (attribute `hide-label`): string, default `Hide password`. Accessible name of the toggle while shown.

Also the properties of RayInput (`<ray-input>`): `value`, `type`, `name`, `label`, `description`, `descriptionPosition`, `error`, `placeholder`, `required`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `size`, `radius`, `variant`.

Events:

- `ray-visibility-change` (detail `{ visible: boolean }`): The user showed or hid the password.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `toggle`: The show/hide button.

### Path input (also File path, Folder picker)

A field for a path on disk: a file to open, a folder, or where to save. In a std/ui window (with ray-elements/core/raylang.js) a Browse… button opens the system dialog; in a browser it is a plain text field. Everything else is ray-input.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/path-input";` · Category: Inputs

#### `<ray-path-input>` (RayPathInput, extends RayInput)

Browse… shows only with a native host that offers pick_path (see core/host.js); the dialog starts in the folder of the current path. The path can always be typed or pasted.

Properties:

- `mode`: `open` | `folder` | `save`, default `open`, reflects. What the dialog chooses: an existing file, a folder, or a file to save (the current name is suggested).
- `accept`: string, reflects. File types the dialog offers, as in <input type=file>: ".json,.toml", "image/*" (ignored for folders).
- `browseLabel` (attribute `browse-label`): string, default `Browse…`. Text of the button.
- `dialogTitle` (attribute `dialog-title`): string. Title of the system dialog (default: the label).

Also the properties of RayInput (`<ray-input>`): `value`, `type`, `name`, `label`, `description`, `descriptionPosition`, `error`, `placeholder`, `required`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `size`, `radius`, `variant`.

Events:

- `change`: The path changed: typed and committed, or chosen in the dialog.
- `ray-error` (detail `{ error: Error }`): The system dialog failed.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `browse`: The Browse… button.

Methods and properties:

- `readonly canBrowse: boolean`: Whether Browse… is available (a native host offers pick_path).
- `browse(): Promise<string | null>`: Opens the system dialog; resolves to the chosen path (also set as value, with input and change), or null.

Exports (from `@raylang/elements/path-input` and `@raylang/elements`):

- `function dirName(path: string): string`: The folder part of a path ("" when it has none), with / or \ separators.
- `function baseName(path: string): string`: The last part of a path.

#### In a raylang app

Browse… shows only in a `std/ui` window with [the native bridge](https://elements.raylang.dev/raylang.html#using-the-bridge). It opens the system's dialog for the `mode`, starting in the folder of the current path (`save` also suggests the current file name). The chosen path fills the field and fires `input` and `change`; the program gets it with the form like any other field.

```html
<ray-path-input name="workspace" label="Workspace" mode="folder"></ray-path-input>
<ray-path-input name="export" label="Export to" mode="save" accept=".csv"></ray-path-input>
```

```ray
// The program's side: ui.events() through bridge.handle, then the form arrives as usual.
for e in ui.events() {
    if (bridge.handle(e)) {
        continue;
    }
    if (e.kind == "message" && e.tag.starts_with("settings:")) {
        save_settings(e.tag.substring(9, e.tag.len()))?;
    }
}
```

### Radio group

One choice among options: ray-radio (or ray-radio-card) elements inside a ray-radio-group, which is the form control.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/radio";` · Category: Inputs

#### `<ray-radio-group>` (RayRadioGroup, extends FormControl)

Arrow keys move the selection, Tab enters and leaves the group.

Properties:

- `value`: string. Value of the checked radio. Initial: the value attribute, or a radio with the checked attribute.
- `name`: string. Form field name.
- `label`: string. Group label (also its accessible name).
- `description`: string. Help text.
- `descriptionPosition` (attribute `description-position`): `above` | `below`, default `above`, reflects. The description before the control (help first) or after it, with the error (fields in a row stay aligned).
- `error`: string. Error text.
- `required`: boolean. A choice is needed to submit.
- `disabled`: boolean. Disables every radio.
- `orientation`: `vertical` | `horizontal`, default `vertical`, reflects. Layout of the radios.
- `size`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`, default `sm`, reflects. Size of every radio.
- `color`: string. Checked color of every radio.
- `variant`: `filled` | `outline`, default `filled`, reflects. Checked look of every radio: filled circle, or colored ring and dot.

Events:

- `input`: When the user picks a radio.
- `change`: When the user picks a radio.

Slots:

- (default): ray-radio or ray-radio-card elements (may be wrapped in layout elements: a ray-grid of cards).

Methods and properties:

- `readonly radios: RayRadio[]`: The radios (and radio cards) of the group.

Vue `v-model`: `value` (updated on change).

#### `<ray-radio>` (RayRadio, extends RayElement)

Properties:

- `value`: string, reflects. Value given to the group when chosen.
- `checked` (attribute `checked`: the initial value only): boolean. Whether this radio is the group's value; setting it sets the group's value. The checked attribute marks the group's initial value (when the group has no value attribute).
- `label`: string. Label text (or the content).
- `description`: string. Help text under the label.
- `disabled`: boolean. Cannot be chosen.
- `color`: string. Overrides the group color.
- `size`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`. Overrides the group size.
- `variant`: `filled` | `outline`, reflects. Overrides the group variant.

Slots:

- (default): Label content.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `indicator`: The circle.
- `label`: The label.

#### `<ray-radio-card>` (RayRadioCard, extends RayRadio)

A radio drawn as a card: a title (label), a detail (description), an icon, more content; checked, it takes the color's border and light background. Inside a ray-radio-group like a ray-radio (arrow keys, the form, required, disabled); put the cards in a ray-grid for columns.

Properties:

- `hideIndicator` (attribute `hide-indicator`): boolean, reflects. No radio circle: the card's border and background alone show the choice.

Also the properties of RayRadio (`<ray-radio>`): `value`, `checked`, `label`, `description`, `disabled`, `color`, `size`, `variant`.

Slots:

- (default): More content under the description.
- `icon`: An icon before the title.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `root`: The card.
- `icon`: Around the icon slot.

### Search

A search box: icon, clear button, an optional shortcut that focuses it, and a debounced ray-search event. A RayInput, so it has a label and takes part in forms.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/search";` · Category: Inputs

#### `<ray-search>` (RaySearch, extends FieldControl)

Escape clears it (when it has text); Enter fires ray-search at once. JS: clear(), focus().

Properties:

- `value`: string. Current text.
- `placeholder`: string, default `Search…`. Placeholder text.
- `shortcut`: string. Keyboard shortcut that focuses it ("mod+k", "/"; mod = ⌘ on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere). Shown as a hint while empty.
- `debounce`: number, default `200`. Milliseconds of quiet typing before ray-search fires (0: on every keystroke).
- `name`: string, reflects. Form field name.
- `label`: string. Visible label (also the accessible name). Without it, use aria-label.
- `disabled`: boolean. Not editable nor submitted.
- `size`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`, default `sm`, reflects. Height and font size.
- `radius`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl` | `full`. Corner radius.
- `variant`: `default` | `filled` | `unstyled`, default `filled`, reflects. Box style.

Also the properties of FieldControl: `description`, `error`, `required`, `descriptionPosition`.

Events:

- `input`: On every edit (value already updated).
- `ray-search` (detail `{ value: string }`): After `debounce` ms without typing, on Enter, and when cleared.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `input`: The inner <input type=search>.
- `icon`: The search icon.
- `clear`: The clear button.
- `shortcut`: The shortcut hint.
- `wrapper`: The box.

Methods and properties:

- `clear(): void`: Empties the box (fires input and ray-search).

Vue `v-model`: `value` (updated on input).

### Segmented control

One choice among a few, as a segmented row with a sliding indicator. Options from child <option> elements or data. Form-associated.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/segmented-control";` · Category: Inputs

#### `<ray-segmented-control>` (RaySegmentedControl, extends FormControl)

Properties:

- `value`: string. Selected value (default: the first enabled option).
- `data` (property only): `Array<string | { value: string; label?: string; disabled?: boolean }>`. Options as strings or { value, label, disabled }.
- `name`: string. Form field name.
- `color`: string, reflects. Indicator color (default: a raised neutral segment).
- `size`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`, default `sm`, reflects. Height and font size.
- `radius`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl` | `full`. Corner radius.
- `fullWidth` (attribute `full-width`): boolean. Takes the whole width.
- `orientation`: `horizontal` | `vertical`, default `horizontal`, reflects. Direction.
- `disabled`: boolean. Not interactive nor submitted.

Events:

- `input`: The user picked another option.
- `change`: The user picked another option.

Slots:

- (default): <option> elements.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `root`: The row.
- `indicator`: The sliding highlight.
- `control`: Each option button.

Methods and properties:

- `readonly items: Array<{ value: string; label: string; disabled: boolean }>`: The options, from data or the child options.

Vue `v-model`: `value` (updated on change).

### Select

A select with its own dropdown (keyboard, typeahead, groups); options from child <option> elements or the data property. Form-associated.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/select";` · Category: Inputs

#### `<ray-select>` (RaySelect, extends FieldControl)

Properties:

- `value`: string. Selected value.
- `data` (property only): `Array<string | { value: string; label?: string; disabled?: boolean }>`. Options as strings or { value, label, disabled } (instead of child options).
- `placeholder`: string. Shown while nothing is selected (with required, blocks submit).
- `open`: boolean, reflects. The dropdown is shown.
- `name`: string. Form field name.
- `label`: string. Visible label.
- `description`: string. Help text.
- `descriptionPosition` (attribute `description-position`): `above` | `below`, default `above`, reflects. The description before the control (help first) or after it, with the error (fields in a row stay aligned).
- `error`: string. Error text.
- `required`: boolean. Required for form submission.
- `disabled`: boolean. Not interactive nor submitted.
- `size`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`, default `sm`, reflects. Height and font size.
- `variant`: `default` | `filled` | `unstyled`, default `default`, reflects. Box style.

Also the properties of FieldControl: `radius`.

Events:

- `input`: When the selection changes.
- `change`: When the selection changes.
- `ray-open`: The dropdown opened.
- `ray-close`: The dropdown closed.

Slots:

- (default): <option> and <optgroup> elements.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `trigger`: The combobox button showing the selected option.
- `dropdown`: The listbox panel (a popover in the top layer).
- `option`: Each option in the dropdown ([aria-selected], [data-active], [aria-disabled]).
- `select`: The hidden native <select> that holds the value (the model).
- `wrapper`: The box.

Methods and properties:

- `readonly options: HTMLOptionsCollection`: The options of the model select.
- `toggle(force?: boolean): void`: Opens or closes the dropdown.

Vue `v-model`: `value` (updated on change).

### Slider

A native range input (keyboard, touch and screen readers as usual) with label, value display and marks. Form-associated.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/slider";` · Category: Inputs

#### `<ray-slider>` (RaySlider, extends FieldControl)

Properties:

- `value`: number. Current value. The value attribute is the initial one (restored on reset).
- `min`: number, default `0`. Minimum.
- `max`: number, default `100`. Maximum.
- `step`: number, default `1`. Step.
- `name`: string. Form field name.
- `label`: string. Visible label.
- `description`: string. Help text.
- `descriptionPosition` (attribute `description-position`): `above` | `below`, default `above`, reflects. The description before the control (help first) or after it, with the error (fields in a row stay aligned).
- `error`: string. Error text.
- `disabled`: boolean. Not interactive nor submitted.
- `color`: string, reflects. Track and thumb color.
- `size`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`, default `sm`, reflects. Track and thumb size.
- `showValue` (attribute `show-value`): boolean, reflects. Shows the value next to the label.
- `unit`: string. Appended to the shown value and its spoken text (%, px, ms…).
- `marks` (property only): `Array<number | { value: number; label?: string }>`. Labeled ticks under the track.

Also the properties of FieldControl: `required`, `radius`, `variant`.

Events:

- `input`: While dragging.
- `change`: When released.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `input`: The native range input.

Vue `v-model`: `value` (updated on input).

### Switch

An on/off toggle with the same API as Checkbox, announced as a switch.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/switch";` · Category: Inputs

#### `<ray-switch>` (RaySwitch, extends RayCheckbox)

Same properties and events as ray-checkbox (indeterminate does not apply).

Properties:

- `checked` (attribute `checked`: the initial value only): boolean. Current state. The checked attribute is the initial state.
- `value`: string, default `on`. Submitted value when on.
- `name`: string. Form field name.
- `label`: string. Label text (or the content).
- `description`: string. Help text.
- `error`: string. Error text.
- `labelPosition` (attribute `label-position`): `end` | `start` | `right` | `left`, default `end`, reflects. Side of the label: start/end follow the writing direction; left/right are sides of the screen.
- `color`: string. Track color when on.
- `size`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`, default `sm`, reflects. Track size.
- `disabled`: boolean. Not interactive nor submitted.

Also the properties of RayCheckbox (`<ray-checkbox>`): `indeterminate`, `required`, `variant`.
Also the properties of FieldControl: `radius`, `descriptionPosition`.

Events:

- `change`: When the user toggles it.

Slots:

- (default): Label content.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `track`: The track.
- `thumb`: The thumb.

Vue `v-model`: `checked` (updated on change).

### Textarea

A multi-line text field that can grow with its content. Form-associated.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/textarea";` · Category: Inputs

#### `<ray-textarea>` (RayTextarea, extends FieldControl)

Also forwards placeholder, autocomplete, minlength, maxlength, spellcheck and wrap. Initial value: the value attribute or the element's text.

Properties:

- `value`: string. Current value.
- `rows`: number, default `3`. Visible rows (minimum when autosize).
- `autosize`: boolean. Grows with the content.
- `maxRows` (attribute `max-rows`): number. With autosize: stop growing and scroll after this many rows.
- `name`: string. Form field name.
- `label`: string. Visible label.
- `description`: string. Help text.
- `descriptionPosition` (attribute `description-position`): `above` | `below`, default `above`, reflects. The description before the control (help first) or after it, with the error (fields in a row stay aligned).
- `error`: string. Error text.
- `required`: boolean. Required for form submission.
- `disabled`: boolean. Not editable nor submitted.
- `readonly`: boolean. Not editable, still submitted.
- `size`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`, default `sm`, reflects. Font size.
- `variant`: `default` | `filled` | `unstyled`, default `default`, reflects. Box style.

Also the properties of FieldControl: `radius`.

Attributes (forwarded to the inner element):

- `placeholder`: Placeholder text.
- `autocomplete`: Forwarded to the inner textarea.
- `minlength`: Minimum length.
- `maxlength`: Maximum length.
- `wrap`: soft or hard.

Events:

- `input`: On every edit.
- `change`: When an edit is committed.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `textarea`: The inner <textarea>.
- `wrapper`: The box.

Vue `v-model`: `value` (updated on input).

### Bottom nav

The bottom navigation of a phone app (Material's navigation bar, the iOS tab bar): three to five destinations with an icon, a label and a badge, the current one marked by a pill. Links or a value; an action button in the middle; hides on scroll.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/bottom-nav";` · Category: Navigation

#### `<ray-bottom-nav>` (RayBottomNav, extends RayElement)

With href items it marks the link to this page (aria-current="page"); without, it is a control (value, change). Clear of the home indicator (safe-area inset). In a ray-app-shell, put it in the bottom slot.

Properties:

- `value`: string, reflects. The current destination (an item's value, else its href, else its label).
- `label`: string, default `Main`. Accessible name of the navigation.
- `labels`: `always` | `active` | `never`, default `always`, reflects. Which labels show (the others stay for assistive technology).
- `indicator`: `pill` | `line` | `none`, default `pill`, reflects. How the current destination is marked besides its color.
- `color`: string, reflects. A palette color or any CSS color for the current item and the action (default: primary).
- `variant`: `default` | `floating`, default `default`, reflects. default: a bar across the bottom; floating: a rounded bar off the edges.
- `hideOnScroll` (attribute `hide-on-scroll`): boolean, reflects. Slides away while the content scrolls down, back on the way up.
- `fixed`: boolean, reflects. Pinned to the bottom of the window (outside a shell).
- `scrollTarget` (attribute `scroll-target`): string. A selector of the element whose scrolling it follows (default: its shell's, else the window).

Events:

- `change`: The user picked another destination (read value).
- `ray-select` (detail `{ value: string }`): An action item was pressed.

Slots:

- (default): ray-bottom-nav-item elements (3 to 5).

Parts (`::part()`):

- `nav`: The <nav>.

Methods and properties:

- `readonly items: RayBottomNavItem[]`: The items, in order.

Vue `v-model`: `value` (updated on change).

#### `<ray-bottom-nav-item>` (RayBottomNavItem, extends RayElement)

A link with href, else a button. The badge is read with the label ("Messages, 3").

Properties:

- `value`: string, reflects. Its value (default: its href, else its label).
- `label`: string. The label.
- `icon`: `IconName`. An icon of the registry, drawn filled on the current item when it has a filled version (or put one in the icon slot: yours, as it is).
- `href`: string, reflects. Makes it a link.
- `badge`: string. A count or a short text on the icon.
- `dot`: boolean, reflects. A dot on the icon (something new).
- `active`: boolean, reflects. Set by the bar: the current destination.
- `disabled`: boolean, reflects. Not interactive.
- `action`: boolean, reflects. A raised round button ("New"): it fires ray-select on the bar, it is not a destination.

Slots:

- `icon`: A custom icon (a ray-icon, an svg, an avatar).

Parts (`::part()`):

- `item`: The link or button.
- `indicator`: The pill behind the icon.
- `badge`: The badge.
- `label`: The label.

### Breadcrumbs

Where a page sits (Mantine's Breadcrumbs, the WAI-ARIA breadcrumb pattern): links in a labelled nav, the last one the current page. Any separator or a chevron; a long path collapses into an expandable "…".

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/breadcrumbs";` · Category: Navigation

#### `<ray-breadcrumbs>` (RayBreadcrumbs, extends RayElement)

A <nav aria-label="Breadcrumb"> around a list. The last crumb is the current page (aria-current="page") unless one says current.

Properties:

- `separator`: string, default `/`. Text between crumbs ("/", "›", "·") or "chevron" (an icon).
- `maxItems` (attribute `max-items`): number. Longer paths show the first crumb, "…" (a button that expands them) and the last max-items − 1.
- `label`: string, default `Breadcrumb`. Accessible name of the nav.
- `size`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg`, default `sm`, reflects. Font size.

Slots:

- (default): ray-breadcrumb elements.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `nav`: The <nav>.
- `list`: The <ol>.

Methods and properties:

- `readonly items: RayBreadcrumb[]`: The crumbs, in order.
- `expand(): void`: Shows every crumb of a collapsed path.

#### `<ray-breadcrumb>` (RayBreadcrumb, extends RayElement)

A link with href (text without, or when current).

Properties:

- `href`: string, reflects. Where it leads.
- `current`: boolean, reflects. This crumb is the current page (default: the last).

Slots:

- (default): The text.
- `icon`: An icon before the text.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `link`: The link (or the text of the current page).
- `separator`: The separator before it.
- `more`: The "…" button of a collapsed path.

### Document tabs

The tabs of open documents (an editor's, a browser's): closable, with an unsaved mark, all over one shared panel; WAI-ARIA tabs with arrows, Home/End and Delete to close. The app closes them: ray-request-close asks.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/doc-tabs";` · Category: Navigation

#### `<ray-doc-tabs>` (RayDocTabs, extends RayElement)

Unlike ray-tabs, a tab has no panel of its own: they all control the element named by panel, whose content the app fills for the selected one. Closing is the app's: the ×, a middle click or Delete/Backspace fire ray-request-close, and the app removes the tab (after asking about unsaved changes, if it must). When the selected tab is removed, the one at its place is selected (change) and, if the closed tab had the focus, focused. More tabs than width: the bar scrolls sideways, fades the edge that hides tabs (data-overflow-start / data-overflow-end on the host), scrolls with a vertical wheel and keeps the selected tab in view.

Properties:

- `value`: string. Value of the selected tab (default: the first).
- `panel`: string. The id of the shared panel: it gets role=tabpanel and aria-labelledby the selected tab; the tabs get aria-controls.
- `label`: string. Accessible name of the tab list ("Open requests").
- `closeLabel` (attribute `close-label`): string, default `Close`. Tooltip of the ×.
- `dirtyLabel` (attribute `dirty-label`): string, default `Unsaved changes`. What assistive technology hears after the name of a dirty tab.

Events:

- `change`: The selected tab changed: a click, the arrow keys, or the selected tab removed.
- `ray-request-close` (detail `{ value: string; tab: RayDocTab; source: "button" | "middle" | "key" }`): The × was clicked, the tab middle-clicked, or Delete/Backspace pressed on it: remove the tab to close it (not fired for hide-close tabs).

Slots:

- (default): ray-doc-tab elements.
- `end`: After the tabs, outside the scrolling list: a new-tab button.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `list`: The tab list (it scrolls sideways when the tabs do not fit).
- `end`: The end slot's box.

Methods and properties:

- `readonly tabs: RayDocTab[]`: Its tabs, in order.
- `readonly panelElement: HTMLElement | null`: The shared panel, found by the panel id.

#### `<ray-doc-tab>` (RayDocTab, extends RayElement)

A document's tab: an icon or tag (slot left), its name (cut with an ellipsis; give the full one in title), and the × or the unsaved dot.

Properties:

- `value`: string, reflects. Identifies the document (ray-doc-tabs value).
- `dirty`: boolean, reflects. Unsaved changes: a dot in place of the ×, which comes back under the pointer.
- `hideClose` (attribute `hide-close`): boolean, reflects. Cannot be closed: no ×, no middle click, no Delete.

Slots:

- (default): The document's name.
- `left`: An icon or a tag (a file type, an HTTP method).

Parts (`::part()`):

- `label`: The name.
- `left-section`: The left slot's box.
- `close`: The × (pointer only: it is not focusable).
- `dot`: The unsaved mark.

### Nav link

A sidebar/navigation item: icon, label, description, badge, active state, and nested nav links that collapse under it.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/nav-link";` · Category: Navigation

#### `<ray-nav-link>` (RayNavLink, extends RayElement)

A link with href (aria-current=page when active), or a button that toggles its nested links.

Properties:

- `label`: string. Text.
- `description`: string. Second line.
- `href`: string, reflects. Makes it a link (ignored when it has nested links).
- `active`: boolean, reflects. The current page or section.
- `opened`: boolean, reflects. Nested links are shown.
- `disabled`: boolean, reflects. Not interactive.
- `variant`: `light` | `filled` | `subtle`, default `light`, reflects. Style of the active state.
- `color`: string, reflects. Active color.
- `iconOnly` (attribute `icon-only`): boolean, reflects. Only the icon (left section), centered; the label becomes its accessible name and tooltip. A collapsed ray-sidebar sets it.

Events:

- `ray-toggle` (detail `{ opened: boolean }`): Nested links were shown or hidden.

Slots:

- (default): Nested ray-nav-link elements.
- `left`: Icon.
- `right`: Badge or count.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `link`: The inner <a> or <button>.
- `children`: The nested links.

Methods and properties:

- `readonly links: RayNavLink[]`: The nested nav links.

Vue `v-model`: `opened` (updated on ray-toggle).

### Pagination

Page navigation: previous/next, optional first/last, page numbers with ellipses; the number of items stays constant so it does not jump.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/pagination";` · Category: Navigation

#### `<ray-pagination>` (RayPagination, extends RayElement)

JS: setPage(n), next(), previous(), first(), last(); page (clamped value).

Properties:

- `total`: number, default `1`. Number of pages.
- `value`: number, default `1`. Current page (1-based).
- `siblings`: number, default `1`. Pages shown on each side of the current one.
- `boundaries`: number, default `1`. Pages always shown at the start and the end.
- `withEdges` (attribute `with-edges`): boolean, reflects. Adds first/last page buttons.
- `hideControls` (attribute `hide-controls`): boolean, reflects. Hides the previous/next (and first/last) buttons.
- `color`: string, reflects. Color of the current page: a palette color or any CSS color. Default: the primary color.
- `size`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`, default `sm`, reflects. Item size.
- `radius`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl` | `full`. Corner radius of the items.
- `disabled`: boolean, reflects. Not interactive.
- `label`: string, default `Pagination`. Accessible name of the navigation landmark.

Events:

- `change`: The user went to another page (read `value`).

Parts (`::part()`):

- `root`: The <nav> landmark.
- `list`: The list of items.
- `item`: Every button (pages and controls).
- `active`: The current page button.
- `control`: Previous/next/first/last buttons.
- `dots`: An ellipsis.

Methods and properties:

- `readonly page: number`: The current page clamped to 1…total.
- `setPage(page: number): void`: Goes to a page (fires change).
- `next(): void`: Next page.
- `previous(): void`: Previous page.
- `first(): void`: First page.
- `last(): void`: Last page.

Vue `v-model`: `value` (updated on change).

Exports (from `@raylang/elements/pagination` and `@raylang/elements`):

- `function paginationRange(total: number, value: number, siblings?: number, boundaries?: number): Array<number | "dots">`: The items a pagination shows for a page (numbers and "dots").

### Sidebar

The side navigation of an app shell: header, content and footer; on wide screens it collapses to an icon rail, below a breakpoint it becomes an off-canvas drawer. toggle() does the right thing for the screen.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/sidebar";` · Category: Navigation

#### `<ray-sidebar>` (RaySidebar, extends RayElement)

Put ray-sidebar-group + ray-nav-link (with an icon in slot=left) inside. Collapsed, nav links show only their icon (the label becomes the tooltip) and the host has the collapsed attribute, so your own header/footer content can hide with CSS (ray-sidebar[collapsed] .brand-name { display: none }).

Properties:

- `collapsed`: boolean, reflects. Wide screens: an icon rail instead of the full panel.
- `open`: boolean, reflects. Narrow screens: the drawer is shown (modal, focus trapped; Escape, backdrop click or a followed link close it).
- `side`: `start` | `end` | `left` | `right`, default `start`, reflects. The edge it sits on (its border faces the content, its narrow-screen drawer slides from there): start/end follow the writing direction; left/right are sides of the screen.
- `variant`: `sidebar` | `floating`, default `sidebar`, reflects. A panel against the edge, or a floating card with a margin.
- `width`: string. Width when expanded (CSS length). Default 16rem.
- `collapsedWidth` (attribute `collapsed-width`): string. Width of the icon rail. Default 3.5rem.
- `breakpoint`: string, default `48em`. At this viewport width and below, it becomes a drawer.
- `label`: string, default `Sidebar`. Accessible name of its navigation.

Events:

- `ray-toggle` (detail `{ collapsed: boolean; open: boolean; mobile: boolean }`): After toggle().
- `ray-open`: The drawer opened (narrow screens).
- `ray-close`: The drawer closed (narrow screens).

Slots:

- (default): The navigation: ray-sidebar-group and ray-nav-link elements.
- `header`: Top area (brand, workspace switcher).
- `footer`: Bottom area (user, settings).

Parts (`::part()`):

- `panel`: The panel (in the drawer on narrow screens).
- `header`: The header area.
- `content`: The scrolling <nav>.
- `footer`: The footer area.
- `drawer`: The <dialog> used on narrow screens.

Methods and properties:

- `toggle(): void`: Collapses/expands on wide screens; opens/closes the drawer on narrow ones.
- `readonly mobile: boolean`: Whether it is in drawer mode (at or below the breakpoint).

#### `<ray-sidebar-group>` (RaySidebarGroup, extends RayElement)

A titled section of nav links; the title fades out (keeping its height) when the sidebar collapses.

Properties:

- `label`: string. Section title.

Slots:

- (default): ray-nav-link elements.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `label`: The title.
- `items`: The links container.

### Stepper
