A task in steps (Mantine's Stepper): a wizard, a checkout, an onboarding. Numbers or icons, labels, connectors, the content of the active step; loading and error states; completed steps can be revisited.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/stepper";` · Category: Navigation

#### `<ray-stepper>` (RayStepper, extends RayElement)

The steps are a labelled list; the active one has aria-current="step" and each reads "Step 2 of 4: Shipping, completed". Only the active step's content shows; past the last step, the completed slot.

Properties:

- `active`: number, default `0`, reflects. Index of the active step (steps.length: completed).
- `orientation`: `horizontal` | `vertical`, default `horizontal`, reflects. Steps in a row above the content, or in a column beside it.
- `iconPosition` (attribute `icon-position`): `start` | `top` | `left`, default `start`, reflects. Label beside the number (after it in the reading direction), or under it (narrow screens, many steps). "left", its former name, still works.
- `allowStepSelect` (attribute `allow-step-select`): boolean, reflects. Completed steps are buttons that go back to them.
- `linear`: boolean, default `true`. With allow-step-select off, false lets the user jump to any step.
- `size`: `sm` | `md` | `lg`, default `md`, reflects. Size of the numbers.
- `color`: string, reflects. A palette color or any CSS color for active and completed steps (default: primary).
- `label`: string, default `Progress`. Accessible name of the list of steps.

Events:

- `change`: active changed by the user (a step clicked, next(), prev()).

Slots:

- (default): ray-step elements.
- `completed`: Shown once every step is done.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `steps`: The list of steps.
- `step`: A step (also step-done, step-active, step-todo).
- `indicator`: A step's number or icon.
- `label`: A step's label.
- `description`: A step's description.
- `connector`: The line between steps.
- `content`: The content area.

Methods and properties:

- `readonly steps: RayStep[]`: The steps, in order.
- `next(): void`: To the next step (past the last: completed).
- `prev(): void`: To the previous step.

Vue `v-model`: `active` (updated on change).

#### `<ray-step>` (RayStep, extends RayElement)

A step: its header is drawn by the stepper, its content shows while it is active.

Properties:

- `label`: string. The label.
- `description`: string. A line under the label.
- `icon`: string. An icon instead of the number.
- `completedIcon` (attribute `completed-icon`): string. The icon once done (default: check).
- `loading`: boolean, reflects. A spinner instead of the number.
- `error`: string. An error message: red step, the message as its description.
- `disabled`: boolean, reflects. Cannot be selected.

Slots:

- (default): The content shown while it is active.

### Tabs

Tabs and panels (WAI-ARIA tabs pattern): arrows, Home/End, automatic or manual activation.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/tabs";` · Category: Navigation

#### `<ray-tabs>` (RayTabs, extends RayElement)

More tabs than width: the list scrolls sideways, fades the edge that hides tabs, scrolls with a vertical wheel and keeps the selected tab in view. The host then carries data-overflow-start and data-overflow-end (following the writing direction), to style it further.

Properties:

- `value`: string. Value of the active tab (default: the first enabled one).
- `variant`: `default` | `outline` | `pills`, default `default`, reflects. Tab style.
- `orientation`: `horizontal` | `vertical`, default `horizontal`, reflects. Tab list direction (and arrow keys).
- `color`: string, reflects. Active indicator color.
- `activation`: `auto` | `manual`, default `auto`. manual: arrows move focus, Enter/Space activates.
- `grow`: boolean, reflects. Tabs share the full width.

Events:

- `change`: The user activated another tab.

Slots:

- (default): ray-tab and ray-tab-panel elements (tabs move to the tab list on their own).

Parts (`::part()`):

- `list`: The tab list (it scrolls sideways when the tabs do not fit).
- `panels`: The panel area.

Methods and properties:

- `readonly tabs: RayTab[]`: The tabs.
- `readonly panels: RayTabPanel[]`: The panels.

Vue `v-model`: `value` (updated on change).

#### `<ray-tab>` (RayTab, extends RayElement)

Properties:

- `value`: string, reflects. Matches a ray-tab-panel's value.
- `disabled`: boolean, reflects. Cannot be activated.

Slots:

- `left`: Icon.
- `right`: Badge or count.

#### `<ray-tab-panel>` (RayTabPanel, extends RayElement)

Properties:

- `value`: string, reflects. Matches a ray-tab's value.

### Command palette

Search and run actions from the keyboard (Mantine's Spotlight): fuzzy search, groups, shortcuts, ⌘K / Ctrl+K; combobox + listbox pattern in a modal dialog.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/command-palette";` · Category: Overlays

#### `<ray-command-palette>` (RayCommandPalette, extends RayElement)

Running an action fires ray-select and calls its onSelect. The best matches come first, grouped.

Properties:

- `open`: boolean, reflects. Shown.
- `actions` (property only): `CommandAction[]`. The actions.
- `query`: string. The search text.
- `placeholder`: string, default `Search commands…`. Placeholder of the search field.
- `hotkey`: string, default `mod+k`. Toggle shortcut (mod = ⌘ on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere); empty to disable.
- `limit`: number, default `50`. Maximum results.
- `emptyLabel` (attribute `empty-label`): string, default `Nothing found`. Text without results.
- `label`: string, default `Command palette`. Accessible name.
- `hideHint` (attribute `hide-hint`): boolean, reflects. No keyboard hint at the bottom.
- `nativeMenus` (attribute `native-menus`): boolean, reflects. With a native host (ray-elements/core/raylang.js in a std/ui window, menus declared with elements/bridge), also lists the app's menu bar, grouped by menu with its shortcuts; running one gives the program the menu's own event.
- `overlayBlur` (attribute `overlay-blur`): string. Blur of the page behind: px ("8"), a CSS length or "none". Default: --ray-overlay-blur ([overlay] blur in tokens.toml).

Events:

- `ray-select` (detail `{ action: CommandAction }`): An action was run.
- `ray-open`: After it opened.
- `ray-close`: After it closed.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `dialog`: The dialog.
- `input`: The search field.
- `option`: Each result.

Methods and properties:

- `show(): void`: Opens it.
- `hide(): void`: Closes it.
- `toggle(): void`: Opens or closes it.
- `readonly results: CommandAction[]`: The actions matching the query, in display order.

Vue `v-model`: `open` (updated on ray-open, ray-close).

Exports (from `@raylang/elements/command-palette` and `@raylang/elements`):

- `function score(action: CommandAction, query: string): number`: How well an action matches a query (0 = not at all).

Types:

- `{ id?: string; label: string; description?: string; group?: string; keywords?: string | string[]; shortcut?: string; icon?: string | Node; disabled?: boolean; native?: boolean; tag?: string; onSelect?: (action: CommandAction) => void }`: An action of ray-command-palette.

#### In a raylang app

With `native-menus` and [the native bridge](https://elements.raylang.dev/raylang.html#using-the-bridge), the palette also lists the app's menu bar: every item, grouped by its menu, with its shortcut, the disabled ones greyed out. Running one gives the program the same `"menu"` event as choosing it in the menu bar, so the program handles it in one place.

```ray
let n = bridge.system();
bridge.menu(n, "File", [ui.item("new", "New window", "cmd+n"), ui.item("open", "Open…", "cmd+o")])?;
for raw in ui.events() {
    let e = match (bridge.route(n, raw)) {
        Option.Some(e) => e,
        Option.None => continue,
    };
    if (e.kind == "menu" && e.tag == "new") {
        new_window()?;
    }
}
```

```html
<ray-command-palette native-menus></ray-command-palette>
```

Declare the menus with `bridge.menu` (and change them with `bridge.replace_menu` and `bridge.set_menu_item`) so the palette knows them.

### Dialog (also Modal)

ray-elements's modal, on the native <dialog>: top layer, the rest of the page inert, focus trapped and restored, stackable. Title, description, header, body and footer; preset or free sizes. Also exports confirmDialog().

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/dialog";` · Category: Overlays

#### `<ray-dialog>` (RayDialog, extends RayElement)

Any slotted element with data-dialog-close closes it (its value becomes returnValue). JS: show(), close(returnValue), confirmDialog({ label, message, confirmLabel, cancelLabel, color, native }) -> Promise<boolean>; with a native host (ray-elements/core/raylang.js in a std/ui window) it asks with the system dialog unless native is false.

Properties:

- `open`: boolean, reflects. Shown as a modal.
- `label`: string. Heading (also the dialog's accessible name).
- `description`: string. A line under the title (the dialog's accessible description).
- `size`: `"xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "full" | (string & {})`, default `md`, reflects. Width: xs…xl, full (the whole window), or any CSS length; a percentage is of the window (70% = 70vw, at least 40rem). Never wider than the window.
- `height`: string, reflects. Fixed height (the body scrolls): any CSS length; a percentage is of the window (70% = 70dvh, at least 30rem). Never taller than the window. Default: as tall as the content, up to the window.
- `radius`: string, reflects. Corner radius: xs…xl, none, or a CSS length. Default: lg.
- `position`: `center` | `top`, default `center`, reflects. Vertical placement.
- `persistent`: boolean, reflects. Escape and backdrop clicks do not close it (the × still does; hide it with hide-close). To allow only one of them, cancel ray-request-close by its source.
- `hideClose` (attribute `hide-close`): boolean, reflects. No close button in the header.
- `overlayBlur` (attribute `overlay-blur`): string. Blur of the page behind: px ("8"), a CSS length or "none". Default: --ray-overlay-blur ([overlay] blur in tokens.toml).

Events:

- `ray-open`: After it opened.
- `ray-close` (detail `{ returnValue: string }`): After it closed; detail: { returnValue }.
- `ray-request-close` (detail `{ source: "escape" | "backdrop" | "button" }`): Escape, backdrop or close button; cancelable (preventDefault keeps it open). detail: { source }.

Slots:

- (default): Body.
- `header`: Extra header content, next to the title.
- `footer`: Actions, aligned to the end.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `dialog`: The native <dialog>.
- `title`: The heading.
- `description`: The line under the heading.
- `header`: The header: title, description, the header slot and the close button.
- `body`: The scrollable body.
- `footer`: The footer.
- `close`: The close button.

Methods and properties:

- `show(): void`: Opens it.
- `close(returnValue?: string): void`: Closes it with an optional return value.
- `returnValue: string`: The value it was closed with.

Vue `v-model`: `open` (updated on ray-open, ray-close).

Exports (from `@raylang/elements/dialog` and `@raylang/elements`):

- `function confirmDialog(options?: ConfirmOptions): Promise<boolean>`: A confirmation dialog; resolves true when confirmed. With a native host, the system dialog (native: false keeps the ray-dialog).

Types:

- `{ label?: string; message?: string; confirmLabel?: string; cancelLabel?: string; color?: string; native?: boolean }`: Options of confirmDialog().

#### In a raylang app

With [the native bridge](https://elements.raylang.dev/raylang.html#using-the-bridge), `confirmDialog()` asks with the system's modal dialog instead of a `ray-dialog`, with the same answer. A red confirmation (a destructive action) gets the warning style. `native: false` keeps the page's dialog, for a question that needs more than a sentence.

```js
if (await confirmDialog({ label: "Delete 3 builds?", message: "This cannot be undone.", confirmLabel: "Delete", color: "red" })) {
  window.ray.send("delete:" + ids.join(","));
}
```

`ray-dialog` itself is always the page's: a form, a settings panel or a wizard stay in the page.

### Drawer

A panel sliding in from an edge: a RayDialog (focus, Escape, persistent, data-dialog-close, returnValue) with another look; modeless for side panels that keep the page interactive.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/drawer";` · Category: Overlays

#### `<ray-drawer>` (RayDrawer, extends RayElement)

Any slotted element with data-dialog-close closes it. JS: show(), close(returnValue).

Properties:

- `open`: boolean, reflects. Shown.
- `label`: string. Heading (also the accessible name).
- `description`: string. A line under the title (the drawer's accessible description).
- `position`: `end` | `start` | `right` | `left` | `top` | `bottom`, default `end`, reflects. The edge it slides from: start/end follow the writing direction; left/right are sides of the screen.
- `size`: `"xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "full" | (string & {})`, default `md`, reflects. Width (left/right) or height (top/bottom): xs…xl, full, or any CSS length.
- `modeless`: boolean, reflects. No backdrop nor scroll lock: the page stays interactive (a side panel).
- `floating`: boolean, reflects. Detached from the edge, with rounded corners.
- `persistent`: boolean, reflects. Escape and backdrop clicks do not close it.
- `hideClose` (attribute `hide-close`): boolean, reflects. No close button in the header.
- `overlayBlur` (attribute `overlay-blur`): string. Blur of the page behind: px ("8"), a CSS length or "none". Default: --ray-overlay-blur ([overlay] blur in tokens.toml).

Events:

- `ray-open`: After it opened.
- `ray-close` (detail `{ returnValue: string }`): After it closed; detail: { returnValue }.
- `ray-request-close` (detail `{ source: "escape" | "backdrop" | "button" }`): Escape, backdrop or close button; cancelable.

Slots:

- (default): Body (scrolls).
- `header`: Extra header content.
- `footer`: Actions, at the bottom.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `drawer`: The native <dialog>.
- `body`: The body.

Methods and properties:

- `show(): void`: Opens it.
- `close(returnValue?: string): void`: Closes it with an optional return value.
- `returnValue: string`: The value it was closed with.

Vue `v-model`: `open` (updated on ray-open, ray-close).

### Menu

A dropdown menu (menu button pattern: arrows, Home/End, typeahead, Enter, Escape) or, with context, a context menu at the pointer.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/menu";` · Category: Overlays

#### `<ray-menu>` (RayMenu, extends Floating)

Properties:

- `open`: boolean, reflects. Shown.
- `placement`: `bottom-start` | `bottom` | `bottom-end` | `top-start` | `top` | `top-end` | `right-start` | `left-start`, default `bottom-start`, reflects. Preferred side and alignment: top/bottom/left/right are sides of the screen; on top and bottom, -start/-end follow the writing direction (right to left, "bottom-start" lines up the right edges).
- `context`: boolean, reflects. Opens on right click (contextmenu) over the trigger area, at the pointer.
- `keepOpen` (attribute `keep-open`): boolean, reflects. Choosing an item does not close the menu.
- `native`: boolean, reflects. With a native host (ray-elements/core/raylang.js in a std/ui window), opens as the system's context menu at the pointer: items and dividers, same ray-select.

Also the properties of Floating: `offset`.

Events:

- `ray-select` (detail `{ value: string; item: RayMenuItem }`): An item was chosen; detail: { value, item }.
- `ray-open`: After it opened.
- `ray-close`: After it closed.

Slots:

- `trigger`: The button that opens it, or the area for a context menu.
- (default): ray-menu-item, ray-menu-label and ray-menu-divider elements.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `dropdown`: The panel.

Methods and properties:

- `popupNative(): Promise<RayMenuItem | null>`: Opens the items as the system's context menu (needs a native host); resolves to the chosen item, or null.
- `show(): void`: Opens it.
- `hide(): void`: Closes it.
- `toggle(): void`: Opens or closes it.
- `readonly trigger: Element | null`: The trigger element.
- `readonly items: RayMenuItem[]`: The items of this menu.

Vue `v-model`: `open` (updated on ray-open, ray-close).

#### `<ray-menu-item>` (RayMenuItem, extends RayElement)

Properties:

- `value`: string, reflects. Reported in ray-select (default: the text).
- `disabled`: boolean, reflects. Skipped by the keyboard, cannot be chosen.
- `color`: string, reflects. Text and hover color (e.g. red for destructive actions).

Slots:

- (default): Label.
- `left`: Icon.
- `right`: Shortcut or badge.

#### `<ray-menu-label>` (RayMenuLabel, extends RayElement)

A section caption inside the menu.

#### `<ray-menu-divider>` (RayMenuDivider, extends RayElement)

A separator between groups of items.

#### In a raylang app

With `native` and [the native bridge](https://elements.raylang.dev/raylang.html#using-the-bridge), the menu opens as the system's context menu at the pointer: its items and dividers, disabled ones greyed out. The choice fires the same `ray-select`, so the same code handles both.

```html
<ray-menu native context>
  <div slot="trigger" class="file-row">report.csv</div>
  <ray-menu-item value="open">Open</ray-menu-item>
  <ray-menu-item value="reveal">Show in Finder</ray-menu-item>
  <ray-menu-divider></ray-menu-divider>
  <ray-menu-item value="delete" color="red">Delete</ray-menu-item>
</ray-menu>
```

Labels, nested menus, icons and colors are the page menu's only. A dismissed native menu fires nothing.

### Popover

A floating panel anchored to a trigger, in the top layer; closes on Escape and outside clicks.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/popover";` · Category: Overlays

#### `<ray-popover>` (RayPopover, extends Floating)

Positioned in JS (flip + shift to stay in the viewport). JS: show(), hide(), toggle().

Properties:

- `open`: boolean, reflects. Shown.
- `placement`: `bottom` | `bottom-start` | `bottom-end` | `top` | `top-start` | `top-end` | `left` | `left-start` | `left-end` | `right` | `right-start` | `right-end`, default `bottom`, reflects. Preferred side and alignment: top/bottom/left/right are sides of the screen; on top and bottom, -start/-end follow the writing direction (right to left, "bottom-start" lines up the right edges).
- `offset`: number, default `8`. Gap to the trigger in px.
- `width`: string. Panel width (px number or CSS length). Default: its content.
- `matchWidth` (attribute `match-width`): boolean. At least as wide as the trigger.
- `padding`: `0` | `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg`, default `md`, reflects. Panel padding.
- `trapFocus` (attribute `trap-focus`): boolean. Moves focus into the panel when opened and keeps Tab inside it.

Events:

- `ray-open`: After it opened.
- `ray-close`: After it closed (also by Escape or an outside click).

Slots:

- `trigger`: The element that toggles it (gets aria-haspopup and aria-expanded).
- (default): Panel content.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `dropdown`: The panel.

Methods and properties:

- `show(): void`: Opens it.
- `hide(): void`: Closes it.
- `toggle(): void`: Opens or closes it.
- `readonly trigger: Element | null`: The trigger element.

Vue `v-model`: `open` (updated on ray-open, ray-close).

### Tooltip

A short hint on hover and focus of its child; the label also becomes the child's accessible description.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/tooltip";` · Category: Overlays

#### `<ray-tooltip>` (RayTooltip, extends Floating)

Properties:

- `label`: string. Tooltip text.
- `placement`: `top` | `bottom` | `left` | `right` | `top-start` | `top-end` | `bottom-start` | `bottom-end`, default `top`, reflects. Preferred side; -start/-end follow the writing direction.
- `openDelay` (attribute `open-delay`): number, default `300`. ms before showing.
- `closeDelay` (attribute `close-delay`): number, default `0`. ms before hiding.
- `color`: string. A palette color or any CSS color. Default: inverted foreground/background.
- `disabled`: boolean. Never shows.

Also the properties of Floating: `open`, `offset`.

Slots:

- (default): The element the tooltip describes (one element).

Parts (`::part()`):

- `tooltip`: The tooltip box.

Methods and properties:

- `show(): void`: Opens it.
- `hide(): void`: Closes it.
- `toggle(): void`: Opens or closes it.
- `readonly trigger: Element | null`: The trigger element.

### Accordion

Collapsible sections (WAI-ARIA accordion pattern); one open at a time, or several with multiple.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/accordion";` · Category: Data display

#### `<ray-accordion>` (RayAccordion, extends RayElement)

Properties:

- `value`: `string | string[] | undefined`. Open item's value; with multiple, an array (attribute: comma-separated).
- `multiple`: boolean, reflects. Several items may be open.
- `variant`: `default` | `contained` | `separated` | `filled`, default `default`, reflects. Visual style.
- `chevronPosition` (attribute `chevron-position`): `end` | `start` | `right` | `left`, default `end`, reflects. Side of the chevron: start/end follow the writing direction; left/right are sides of the screen.

Events:

- `change`: The user opened or closed an item.

Slots:

- (default): ray-accordion-item elements.

Methods and properties:

- `readonly items: RayAccordionItem[]`: The items.
- `readonly openValues: string[]`: The open values as an array, whatever the mode.

Vue `v-model`: `value` (updated on change).

#### `<ray-accordion-item>` (RayAccordionItem, extends RayElement)

Properties:

- `value`: string, reflects. Identifies the item in the accordion's value.
- `label`: string. Header text (or slot=label).
- `description`: string. A secondary line under the label, in the header.
- `disabled`: boolean, reflects. Cannot be toggled.
- `headingLevel` (attribute `heading-level`): number, default `3`. aria-level of the header.

Slots:

- (default): Panel content.
- `label`: Rich header content.
- `left`: Icon before the label.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `control`: The header button.
- `description`: The secondary line under the label.
- `panel`: The collapsible region.

Methods and properties:

- `readonly open: boolean`: Whether this item is expanded.

### Attachment

A file in a composer, upload list or chat: thumbnail or type icon, name, size, upload progress, error, remove and download.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/attachment";` · Category: Data display

#### `<ray-attachment>` (RayAttachment, extends RayElement)

Assign a File to `file` to fill name, size, type and an image thumbnail. Removing it (× button) fires a cancelable ray-remove and then removes the element.

Properties:

- `name`: string, reflects. File name (ellipsized; full name in the tooltip).
- `size`: number. Size in bytes, shown as "12 KB", "3.4 MB".
- `type`: string, reflects. MIME type: picks the icon (image or file) and, with the name, the extension badge.
- `src`: string. Thumbnail URL for images (falls back to the icon if it fails to load).
- `href`: string, reflects. Makes the name a download link.
- `progress`: number. Upload progress 0–100: a thin bar and "Uploading… 45%". Unset: done.
- `status`: `uploading` | `done` | `error`, reflects. Explicit state. Default: "uploading" while progress is set, else "done".
- `error`: string. Error text shown with status="error" (default "Upload failed").
- `removable`: boolean, reflects. Shows a remove (×) button.
- `removeLabel` (attribute `remove-label`): string, default `Remove {name}`. Accessible label of the remove button; {name} is replaced by the file name.
- `variant`: `row` | `card`, default `row`, reflects. row: a compact chip; card: the thumbnail on top.
- `disabled`: boolean, reflects. Dimmed, not removable, the name is not a link.

Events:

- `ray-remove` (detail `{ name: string; file: File | null }`): The remove button was pressed; cancelable (preventDefault keeps the element).

Parts (`::part()`):

- `item`: The box.
- `thumbnail`: The thumbnail or icon box.
- `badge`: The extension badge (PDF, PNG…).
- `name`: The file name (a link with href).
- `meta`: Size, upload state or error.
- `progress`: The upload progress bar.
- `remove`: The remove button.

Methods and properties:

- `file: File | null`: The File shown (fills name, size, type and a thumbnail for images).
- `readonly state: "uploading" | "done" | "error"`: The effective status.

#### `<ray-attachments>` (RayAttachments, extends RayElement)

A wrapping row of ray-attachment elements.

Slots:

- (default): ray-attachment elements.

### Avatar

An image, the initials of a name, or a placeholder icon.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/avatar";` · Category: Data display

#### `<ray-avatar>` (RayAvatar, extends RayElement)

Properties:

- `src`: string, reflects. Image URL; falls back to initials if it fails to load.
- `alt`: string, reflects. Accessible name (default: name).
- `name`: string, reflects. Person or entity name; its initials are shown without an image.
- `color`: string. A palette color or any CSS color.
- `variant`: `light` | `filled` | `outline` | `default`, default `light`, reflects. Style of the initials/placeholder.
- `size`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`, default `md`, reflects. Diameter.
- `radius`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl` | `full`. Corner radius. Default: full.

Slots:

- (default): Custom content (e.g. an icon) instead of initials.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `avatar`: The box.
- `image`: The <img>.

Exports (from `@raylang/elements/avatar` and `@raylang/elements`):

- `function initials(name: string): string`: Up to two initials of a name: "Ada Lovelace" -> "AL".

### Badge

A short status label.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/badge";` · Category: Data display

#### `<ray-badge>` (RayBadge, extends RayElement)

Properties:

- `variant`: `light` | `filled` | `outline` | `dot` | `default` | `gradient`, default `light`, reflects. Visual style.
- `gradient`: string, reflects. With variant=gradient: "from to [deg]", palette colors or CSS colors ("teal blue 90"). Default: the --ray-gradient-* tokens.
- `color`: string. A palette color or any CSS color.
- `size`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`, default `sm`, reflects. Height and font size.
- `radius`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl` | `full`. Corner radius. Default: full.
- `normalCase` (attribute `normal-case`): boolean. Keeps the text as written instead of uppercase.

Slots:

- (default): The text.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `badge`: The badge box.

### Blockquote

A quotation set apart from the text (Mantine's Blockquote): a colored edge, a quote mark on it and the attribution below. A real <blockquote> inside, with the source's URL as its cite.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/blockquote";` · Category: Data display

#### `<ray-blockquote>` (RayBlockquote, extends RayElement)

Paragraphs in it are spaced and the last one has no bottom margin. The attribution is text (cite) or rich content (slot="cite": an avatar, a name, a role).

Properties:

- `cite`: string. Who said it, shown below the quote ("— Grace Hopper").
- `href`: string. URL of the source: the inner blockquote's cite attribute.
- `color`: string, reflects. A palette color or any CSS color, for the edge, the mark and the tint. Default: the primary.
- `variant`: `light` | `outline` | `filled`, default `light`, reflects. light: tinted background; outline: border and edge only; filled: solid color (a pull quote).
- `icon`: `IconName`, default `quote`. Registry icon of the mark, or none. The icon slot replaces it.
- `size`: `sm` | `md` | `lg`, default `md`, reflects. Text size (lg for a pull quote).
- `padding`: string, reflects. Inner spacing: xs…xl (the spacing scale), px as a number, or a CSS length. Default: md.
- `hideEdge` (attribute `hide-edge`): boolean, reflects. No colored edge on the start side (the tint, border and mark stay).
- `radius`: string, reflects. Corner radius: xs…xl, none, or a CSS length. Default: md.

Slots:

- (default): The quotation (text or paragraphs).
- `cite`: Rich attribution, instead of cite.
- `icon`: A custom mark, instead of icon.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `quote`: The <blockquote>.
- `icon`: The disc with the mark.
- `cite`: The attribution (a <figcaption>).

### Carousel

Slides in a scroll-snap viewport: native swipe and scrolling, previous/next controls, indicators, keyboard, loop and autoplay with a pause button.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/carousel";` · Category: Data display

#### `<ray-carousel>` (RayCarousel, extends RayElement)

Any child is a slide. With several slides in view, positions are the snap points the viewport can reach. ArrowLeft/Right (Up/Down when vertical), Home and End move it.

Properties:

- `index`: number, default `0`. Current position (0-based). Setting it scrolls there.
- `label`: string, default `Carousel`. Accessible name of the carousel region.
- `slideSize` (attribute `slide-size`): string. Size of each slide along the scroll axis ("100%" by default; "50%", "18rem"…).
- `slideGap` (attribute `slide-gap`): string. Space between slides (default var(--ray-space-4)).
- `align`: `start` | `center`, default `start`, reflects. Where a slide snaps in the viewport.
- `orientation`: `horizontal` | `vertical`, default `horizontal`, reflects. Scroll axis (vertical needs a height; 20rem by default).
- `loop`: boolean, reflects. next() on the last position goes to the first, prev() on the first to the last.
- `autoplay`: number, default `0`. Milliseconds between automatic moves (0: off). Pauses on hover, focus and when the page is hidden; starts paused with reduced motion. Shows a pause/play button.
- `hideControls` (attribute `hide-controls`): boolean, reflects. No previous/next buttons.
- `hideIndicators` (attribute `hide-indicators`): boolean, reflects. No indicator dots.

Events:

- `change`: The current position changed (read `index`) by the user or a method (controls, indicators, keyboard, swipe, scroll, next/prev/goTo, autoplay) — not when `index` is set by code.

Slots:

- (default): The slides.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `viewport`: The scrolling viewport.
- `previous`: The previous button.
- `next`: The next button.
- `indicators`: The row of indicator dots.
- `indicator`: Each indicator dot ([aria-current] on the active one).
- `play`: The pause/play button (with autoplay).

Methods and properties:

- `next(): void`: Goes to the next position.
- `prev(): void`: Goes to the previous position.
- `goTo(index: number, options?: { instant?: boolean }): void`: Scrolls to a position (smoothly unless instant or reduced motion).
- `readonly count: number`: Number of positions.
- `readonly slides: Element[]`: The slide elements.

### Code

A block of source code: header with file name and language, copy button, line numbers, highlighted lines, diff lines, wrapping and a "show more" height. A small built-in highlighter, or any library through setHighlighter(), painted with the --ray-code-* tokens.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/code";` · Category: Data display

#### `<ray-code>` (RayCode, extends RayElement)

The code comes from the code property, a <script type="text/plain"> child (raw text: anything but a closing script tag), a <template> child (parsed as HTML: the easiest for markup, but a < that is not a tag, as in Promise<void>, breaks it), or the element's text; common indentation and blank edges are removed. Built-in languages: js/ts (jsx, tsx), json, html/xml/svg/vue, css, shell, ray and diff; others show as plain text. Library classes painted with the tokens: Prism's .token.*, highlight.js's .hljs-*, and Shiki's css-variables theme.

Properties:

- `code` (property only): string. The code, from script (the most convenient in React and Vue). Wins over the content.
- `language`: string, reflects. The language: js, ts, jsx, tsx, json, html, xml, svg, vue, css, sh, ray, diff… (also shown in the header). Not lang: that is the human language of the text.
- `filename`: string. A file name or title in the header; also the scroll region's accessible name.
- `lineNumbers` (attribute `line-numbers`): boolean, reflects. Numbers each line (not copied, not selectable).
- `highlight`: string. Lines to highlight: "3, 5-7".
- `wrap`: boolean, reflects. Wraps long lines instead of scrolling sideways.
- `maxHeight` (attribute `max-height`): string. Height before it scrolls: px as a number, or a CSS length. A taller block gets a "Show all N lines" button.
- `expanded`: boolean, reflects. Shown whole, past max-height.
- `hideCopy` (attribute `hide-copy`): boolean, reflects. No copy button.
- `hideHeader` (attribute `hide-header`): boolean, reflects. No header bar (the copy button floats in the corner).
- `size`: `xs` | `sm` | `md`, default `sm`, reflects. Font size.
- `radius`: string, reflects. Corner radius: xs…xl, none, or a CSS length. Default: md.
- `copyLabel` (attribute `copy-label`): string, default `Copy code`. Accessible name of the copy button.
- `copiedLabel` (attribute `copied-label`): string, default `Copied`. Shown and announced after copying.

Events:

- `ray-copy` (detail `{ code: string }`): The code was copied.

Slots:

- (default): The code: text, a <template> or a <script type="text/plain">.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `frame`: The box.
- `header`: The bar with the file name, the language and the copy button.
- `copy`: The copy button.
- `scroller`: The scroll box (focusable, to scroll with the keyboard).
- `code`: The <code> with one .line per line.

Methods and properties:

- `readonly source: string`: The code shown (dedented), whatever its source.
- `copy(): Promise<boolean>`: Copies the code; resolves to true when it worked.

Exports (from `@raylang/elements/code` and `@raylang/elements`):

- `function setHighlighter(fn: ((code: string, lang: string) => string | Node | null | undefined | Promise<string | Node | null | undefined>) | null): void`: Hands every ray-code to a highlighter that returns HTML (Prism, highlight.js, Shiki…); null/undefined falls back to the built-in one. The HTML is inserted as is: pass only a trusted highlighter. null restores the built-in one.
- `function tokenize(code: string, lang?: string): [type: string, text: string][]`: The built-in highlighter: tokens of type keyword, string, number, comment, function, type, tag, attr, punctuation or text.

### Icon

An icon of the registry: the whole set (the components' too) changes with setIcons().

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/icon";` · Category: Data display

#### `<ray-icon>` (RayIcon, extends RayElement)

setIcons({ name: '<svg…>' }) replaces or adds icons (SVG markup or an SVGElement, drawn with currentColor); iconNames() lists them. An icon may have a filled version for a state (filled; "<name>:filled" in setIcons; iconNames({ filled: true }) lists them). The components draw roles ("ui.close", "ui.remove", "ui.expand"…; iconAliases()), each its glyph until the app registers the role: setIcons({ "ui.remove": … }) changes only the chips' ×. Sizes follow the font unless size; --ray-icon-size and --ray-icon-stroke tune the whole system.

Properties:

- `name`: `IconName`, reflects. Registered icon name (iconNames()); "none" draws nothing, a blank that keeps the alignment (a menu item without its check).
- `filled`: boolean, reflects. The filled version, for a state (active, selected, favorite, unread); the outline icon when there is none. Built in: user, info, circle-check, alert-triangle, circle-x, folder, bell, star, settings, home, message-circle.
- `mirror`: boolean, reflects. Mirrored in a right-to-left context (dir="rtl"), for an icon that points along the text: back, forward, send, undo. The roles that do (ui.next, ui.previous, ui.first, ui.last, ui.disclosure, ui.separator) mirror by themselves.
- `size`: string, reflects. xs…xl or any CSS length. Default: 1em.
- `label`: string. Accessible name; without it the icon is decorative (hidden from screen readers).
- `color`: string, reflects. A palette color or any CSS color. Default: the text color.
- `stroke`: number. Stroke width for stroke icons (default: --ray-icon-stroke, 2).

Parts (`::part()`):

- `icon`: The icon box.

Types:

- `"close" | "check" | "minus" | "plus" | "chevron-down" | "chevron-up" | "chevron-right" | "chevron-left" | "chevrons-left" | "chevrons-right" | "search" | "arrow-up-right" | "arrow-down-right" | "sun" | "moon" | "monitor" | "user" | "info" | "circle-check" | "alert-triangle" | "circle-x" | "menu" | "more-horizontal" | "file" | "folder" | "pause" | "play" | "terminal" | "calendar" | "image" | "download" | "eye" | "eye-off" | "bell" | "copy" | "quote" | "pipette" | "star" | "upload" | "paperclip" | "panel-left" | "settings" | "home" | "arrow-left" | "message-circle" | "none" | (string & {})`: An icon name: one of the default set, or any name an app registers with setIcons().

### Indicator

A dot or a small label on the edge of any element (Mantine's Indicator): "New" on an avatar, an unread count on a bell, an online dot. Nine positions, an inward offset, palette or CSS colors, a border and a live pulse.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/indicator";` · Category: Data display

#### `<ray-indicator>` (RayIndicator, extends RayElement)

Wraps its content as tight as it is (fit-content). The label is part of the element's text for assistive technology; a dot has none: describe it on the content (aria-label="Grace, online").

Properties:

- `label`: string. Text in the indicator (a word or a count). Empty: a dot.
- `position`: `top-start` | `top-center` | `top-end` | `middle-start` | `middle-center` | `middle-end` | `bottom-start` | `bottom-center` | `bottom-end`, default `top-end`, reflects. Which point of the content's box it sits on.
- `offset`: `string | number`. Moves it inward from that point: px as a number, or a CSS length. Use it on round content (an avatar), so it sits on the curve.
- `color`: string, reflects. A palette color or any CSS color. Default: the primary.
- `size`: `string | number`. Diameter of the dot (and minimum height of a label): px as a number, or a CSS length. Default: 10px.
- `radius`: string, reflects. Corner radius: xs…xl, none, or a CSS length. Default: round.
- `max`: number. A numeric label above it shows as max+ (99+).
- `inline`: boolean, reflects. inline-block, to sit within a line of text.
- `withBorder` (attribute `with-border`): boolean, reflects. A ring in the background color, to separate it from the content.
- `processing`: boolean, reflects. A pulse around it (live, recording, syncing).
- `disabled`: boolean, reflects. Hides the indicator (the content stays).

Slots:

- (default): The element the indicator sits on.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `indicator`: The dot or label.

### Kbd

A keyboard key: a raised keycap, or a flat chip (filled or outline) for hints in menus and buttons.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/kbd";` · Category: Data display

#### `<ray-kbd>` (RayKbd, extends RayElement)

Properties:

- `size`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`, default `sm`, reflects. Font size.
- `variant`: `default` | `filled` | `outline`, default `default`, reflects. default: raised keycap; filled: flat muted chip; outline: flat with a border.

Slots:

- (default): The key name.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `kbd`: The inner <kbd>.

### Stat

A metric tile: label, value, change against a previous period, note.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/stat";` · Category: Data display

#### `<ray-stat>` (RayStat, extends RayElement)

Properties:

- `label`: string. What is measured.
- `value`: string. The figure, already formatted.
- `diff`: number. Change (positive is shown as good, in green; see inverse).
- `diffUnit` (attribute `diff-unit`): string, default `%`. Unit of diff.
- `note`: string. A line under the value (compared to…).
- `inverse`: boolean, reflects. Lower is better (errors, latency): negative diffs are green.
- `plain`: boolean, reflects. Without the card around.

Slots:

- `icon`: Icon next to the label.
- (default): Extra content (e.g. a ray-progress).

### Table

A data table from columns and data: sorting (aria-sort), row selection, clickable rows, sticky header, striped, empty state. Plain HTML tables: the .ray-table class of base.css.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/table";` · Category: Data display

#### `<ray-table>` (RayTable, extends RayElement)

Cells are text (render may return a DOM node; strings are never parsed as HTML). The scroll height comes from --ray-table-max-height.

Properties:

- `columns` (property only): `TableColumn[]`. Columns: key, label, width, align, sortable, render(row, index), sort(a, b).
- `data` (property only): `any[]`. Rows (objects).
- `rowKey` (attribute `row-key`): string, default `id`. Field that identifies a row (selection).
- `selectable`: boolean, reflects. A checkbox per row and a select-all checkbox.
- `selection` (property only): `unknown[]`. Keys of the selected rows.
- `sort` (property only): `TableSort | null`. Current sort; set it, or let header clicks change it.
- `manualSort` (attribute `manual-sort`): boolean. Do not sort here: listen to ray-sort and pass sorted data.
- `clickableRows` (attribute `clickable-rows`): boolean, reflects. Rows are focusable and fire ray-row-click (Enter too; arrows move between rows).
- `striped`: boolean, reflects. Alternate row background.
- `withBorder` (attribute `with-border`): boolean, reflects. Border around the table.
- `withColumnBorders` (attribute `with-column-borders`): boolean, reflects. Borders between columns.
- `stickyHeader` (attribute `sticky-header`): boolean, reflects. The header stays visible while scrolling (with --ray-table-max-height).
- `noHover` (attribute `no-hover`): boolean, reflects. No row highlight on hover.
- `density`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg`, default `sm`, reflects. Cell padding.
- `label`: string. Caption (also the table's accessible name).
- `emptyLabel` (attribute `empty-label`): string, default `No data`. Text without rows (or put a ray-empty-state in slot=empty).

Events:

- `ray-sort` (detail `{ key: string; direction: "asc" | "desc" | null }`): A header changed the sort.
- `ray-selection-change` (detail `{ selection: unknown[] }`): The selection changed.
- `ray-row-click` (detail `{ row: any; index: number }`): A row was clicked or activated with Enter (clickable-rows).

Slots:

- `empty`: Shown instead of the empty text when there are no rows.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `table`: The <table>.
- `scroll`: The scroll container.

Methods and properties:

- `readonly rows: any[]`: The rows in display order.

Types:

- `{ key: string; label?: string; width?: number | string; align?: "left" | "center" | "right"; sortable?: boolean; render?: (row: any, index: number) => string | number | Node | null | undefined; sort?: (a: any, b: any) => number }`: A column of ray-table.
- `{ key: string; direction: "asc" | "desc" }`: The sort state of ray-table.

### Timeline

Events in order along a line (Mantine's Timeline): activity, history, a deploy's stages. Items up to active are reached (filled bullet, colored line); a bullet is a dot, an icon or an avatar.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/timeline";` · Category: Data display

#### `<ray-timeline>` (RayTimeline, extends RayElement)

A list (role="list") of ray-timeline-item.

Properties:

- `active`: number, default `-1`, reflects. Index of the last reached item (-1: none).
- `align`: `start` | `end` | `left` | `right`, default `start`, reflects. Side of the line: start/end follow the writing direction; left/right are sides of the screen.
- `bulletSize` (attribute `bullet-size`): string. Bullet size: px as a number or a CSS length (default 20px).
- `lineWidth` (attribute `line-width`): number. Line width in px (default 2).
- `color`: string, reflects. A palette color or any CSS color for what is reached (default: primary).
- `reverseActive` (attribute `reverse-active`): boolean, reflects. Counts active from the end (the latest event at the top).

Slots:

- (default): ray-timeline-item elements.

Methods and properties:

- `readonly items: RayTimelineItem[]`: The items, in order.

#### `<ray-timeline-item>` (RayTimelineItem, extends RayElement)

Properties:

- `label`: string. The title of the event.
- `time`: string. When ("2 h ago", a date).
- `icon`: `IconName`. An icon of the registry in the bullet.
- `color`: string, reflects. Its own color (a failed step in red).
- `lineVariant` (attribute `line-variant`): `solid` | `dashed` | `dotted`, default `solid`, reflects. The line to the next item (dashed: not happened yet).

Slots:

- (default): Details under the title.
- `bullet`: A custom bullet (an avatar, an image).

Parts (`::part()`):

- `bullet`: The bullet.
- `line`: The line to the next item.
- `body`: Title, details and time.
- `title`: The title.
- `time`: The time.

### Alert

An inline message: title, text, an icon of the registry, the color variants and an optional close button.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/alert";` · Category: Feedback

#### `<ray-alert>` (RayAlert, extends RayElement)

Announced as an alert. The icon follows the color (info, circle-check, alert-triangle, circle-x) unless icon or slot=icon.

Properties:

- `label`: string. Title.
- `color`: string, reflects. A palette color or any CSS color.
- `variant`: `light` | `filled` | `outline` | `default` | `transparent`, default `light`, reflects. Visual style.
- `radius`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`. Corner radius.
- `icon`: `IconName`, reflects. A registered icon name, or none.
- `closable`: boolean, reflects. A close button; closing hides the alert (cancel ray-close to keep it).
- `closeLabel` (attribute `close-label`): string, default `Dismiss`. Accessible name of the close button.

Events:

- `ray-close`: The close button was pressed; cancelable.

Slots:

- (default): Text.
- `icon`: A custom icon.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `alert`: The box.
- `close`: The close button.

### Empty state

What a list, table or pane shows when it is empty: icon, title, text and the action that fills it.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/empty-state";` · Category: Feedback

#### `<ray-empty-state>` (RayEmptyState, extends RayElement)

Properties:

- `label`: string. Title.
- `compact`: boolean, reflects. Less padding.
- `withBorder` (attribute `with-border`): boolean, reflects. Dashed border.

Slots:

- (default): Text.
- `icon`: Icon, shown in a circle.
- `actions`: Buttons.

### Notification

Toasts: notify(), updateNotification(), hideNotification(), clearNotifications(); shown in a ray-toaster (a polite live region in the top layer). ray-notification is usable on its own.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/notification";` · Category: Feedback

#### `<ray-notification>` (RayNotification, extends RayElement)

notify({ id, title, message, color, icon, loading, autoClose (ms, default 4000; false = stays), closable, withBorder, onClose }) returns its id. A color adds a status icon in that color: green/teal a check, red/pink an error, yellow/orange a warning, others info. The status icon and the loader are 1.5rem with a 1.5 stroke; set --ray-notification-icon-size and --ray-notification-icon-stroke to change them.

Properties:

- `label`: string. Title.
- `color`: string, reflects. Status color: tints the status icon (and a slotted icon's circle).
- `icon`: `IconName`. Status icon from the registry (default: from the color); "none" for no icon.
- `loading`: boolean, reflects. Shows a spinner (notify() does not auto-close it).
- `hideClose` (attribute `hide-close`): boolean, reflects. No close button.
- `withBorder` (attribute `with-border`): boolean, reflects. Draws a border.
- `actionLabel` (attribute `action-label`): string. Text of an action button (e.g. "Undo"); pressing it fires ray-action.

Events:

- `ray-close`: The close button was pressed.
- `ray-action`: The action button was pressed (notify() runs action.onClick and closes it).

Slots:

- (default): Message.
- `icon`: Your own icon, in a colored circle (replaces the status icon).

Parts (`::part()`):

- `status-icon`: The status icon.

#### `<ray-toaster>` (RayToaster, extends RayElement)

Created by notify() when missing; add one yourself to choose its position. A stack (newest in front, older ones peeking behind) that spreads into a list on hover or keyboard focus; on touch screens a tap expands it, a tap outside collapses it, and a sideways swipe dismisses a toast. Auto-close pauses while expanded. Full width on phones.

Properties:

- `position`: `bottom-end` | `bottom-start` | `bottom-center` | `top-end` | `top-start` | `top-center` | `bottom-right` | `bottom-left` | `top-right` | `top-left`, default `bottom-end`, reflects. Corner of the stack: -start/-end follow the writing direction; -left/-right are sides of the screen.
- `limit`: number, default `5`. Maximum kept; the oldest go first.
- `visible`: number, default `3`. Toasts shown in the collapsed stack (the rest wait, hidden).
- `expand`: boolean, reflects. Always expanded: a list instead of a stack.
- `gap`: number, default `12`. Pixels between toasts when expanded.

Methods and properties:

- `expanded: boolean`: Whether the stack is spread out (set it to expand or collapse it).
- `layout(): void`: Places the toasts again (done automatically on changes).
- `raise(): void`: Brings the stack above everything else in the top layer.

Exports (from `@raylang/elements/notification` and `@raylang/elements`):

- `function notify(options?: NotifyOptions): string`: Shows a notification; returns its id.
- `function updateNotification(id: string, options?: NotifyOptions): boolean`: Changes a shown notification and restarts its auto-close.
- `function hideNotification(id: string): boolean`: Removes a notification.
- `function clearNotifications(): void`: Removes every notification.
- `function statusIcon(color: string): string`: The status icon a color gets: circle-check, circle-x, alert-triangle or info.

Types:

- `{ id?: string; title?: string; message?: string; color?: string; icon?: string; loading?: boolean; autoClose?: number | false; closable?: boolean; withBorder?: boolean; action?: { label: string; onClick?: () => void }; onClose?: () => void }`: Options of notify() and updateNotification().

### Progress

A determinate or (without value) indeterminate progress bar, announced as a progressbar.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/progress";` · Category: Feedback

#### `<ray-progress>` (RayProgress, extends RayElement)

Properties:

- `value`: number. Progress, from 0 to max. Unset: indeterminate.
- `max`: number, default `100`. The value of a full bar.
- `color`: string, reflects. A palette color or any CSS color.
- `size`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`, default `md`, reflects. Bar height.
- `radius`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl` | `full`. Corner radius. Default: full.
- `striped`: boolean, reflects. Diagonal stripes.
- `animated`: boolean, reflects. Moving stripes (with striped).
- `showValue` (attribute `show-value`): boolean, reflects. Shows the percentage: inside the bar on lg and xl, beside it on smaller sizes.
- `label`: string. Accessible name (default: Progress).

Parts (`::part()`):

- `track`: The background track.
- `bar`: The filled bar.
- `value`: The percentage beside the bar (show-value on xs, sm, md).

### Ring progress

Progress as a ring (Mantine's RingProgress), with content in the middle: a countdown, a goal, an upload. Announced as a progressbar.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/ring-progress";` · Category: Feedback

#### `<ray-ring-progress>` (RayRingProgress, extends RayElement)

The arc starts at 12 o'clock and runs clockwise; a countdown is a value that goes down. Without value it spins (indeterminate). The middle holds the default slot (a clock), or the percentage with show-value.

Properties:

- `value`: number. Progress, from 0 to max. Unset: indeterminate (a spinning arc).
- `max`: number, default `100`. The value of a full ring.
- `color`: string, reflects. A palette color or any CSS color. Default: the primary color.
- `size`: `"xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | (string & {})`, default `md`, reflects. Diameter: xs…xl (3, 5, 7.5, 10, 12.5rem) or any CSS length.
- `thickness`: string, reflects. Width of the ring: a CSS length (a bare number is px). Default: a tenth of the diameter.
- `roundCaps` (attribute `round-caps`): boolean, reflects. Rounded ends of the arc.
- `showValue` (attribute `show-value`): boolean, reflects. Shows the percentage in the middle (when the default slot is empty).
- `label`: string. Accessible name (default: Progress).

Slots:

- (default): The middle of the ring (a clock, a figure, an icon); its font scales with size.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `track`: The background circle.
- `bar`: The arc.
- `center`: The middle, around the default slot.

### Skeleton

A placeholder while content loads: a shimmering block, a circle or text lines; with loaded it shows its content.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/skeleton";` · Category: Feedback

#### `<ray-skeleton>` (RaySkeleton, extends RayElement)

aria-busy="true" on the host while loading; the placeholder is aria-hidden.

Properties:

- `width`: string. Width (CSS length, a number is px). Default: 100% (a circle: 2.5rem).
- `height`: string. Height of a block or of each line (CSS length, a number is px). Default: 1rem.
- `circle`: boolean, reflects. A circle (avatar placeholder): its diameter is width, else height.
- `lines`: number, reflects. Number of text lines (the last one is shorter).
- `radius`: string, reflects. Corner radius: xs…xl, full or a CSS length. Default: sm.
- `animation`: `shimmer` | `pulse` | `none`, default `shimmer`, reflects. The loading effect (always none with reduced motion).
- `loaded`: boolean, reflects. Shows the slotted content instead of the placeholder.

Slots:

- (default): The real content, shown with loaded.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `skeleton`: The placeholder container.
- `bone`: Each block or line.

### Spinner

An indeterminate loading indicator, announced as a status.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/spinner";` · Category: Feedback

#### `<ray-spinner>` (RaySpinner, extends RayElement)

Properties:

- `color`: string. A palette color or any CSS color. Default: the primary color.
- `size`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`, default `md`, reflects. Diameter.
- `label`: string, default `Loading`. Text read by screen readers.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `spinner`: The ring.

### Step dots

A row of dots, one per step: done, current, to do. A compact progress for rounds, onboarding pages or a quiz; announced as a progressbar ("Round 4 of 12").

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/step-dots";` · Category: Feedback

#### `<ray-step-dots>` (RayStepDots, extends RayElement)

Dots before value are done (filled), the one at value is current (a filled pill), the rest are to do (empty). Not interactive: for steps the user picks, use ray-stepper (or the dots of ray-carousel). Many dots wrap onto more lines.

Properties:

- `count`: number, default `0`. Number of steps (dots).
- `value`: number, default `0`. The current step, 0-based; count means every step is done.
- `color`: string, reflects. A palette color or any CSS color for done and current dots. Default: the primary color.
- `size`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`, default `sm`, reflects. Size of a dot.
- `align`: `start` | `center` | `end`, default `center`, reflects. Where the row sits in its width.
- `label`: string. What a step is called: "Round" is announced "Round 4 of 12" and names the element. Default: Step (named Steps). In another language, use value-text.
- `valueText` (attribute `value-text`): string. The announced text, {step} (the current one, from 1) and {count} replaced, numbers in the page's language: value-text="Asalto {step} de {count}". Default: "<label> {step} of {count}".
- `doneText` (attribute `done-text`): string. The announced text once every step is done (value = count), with {count}. Default: value-text, else "{count} of {count}, done".

Parts (`::part()`):

- `dots`: The row.
- `dot`: Each dot ([data-state] done, current or todo).

### App bar

The top bar of a phone screen (Material's top app bar, the iOS navigation bar): back or menu, a title and subtitle, actions, and an optional row under it. It elevates once the content scrolls, or hides while scrolling down.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/app-bar";` · Category: Layout

#### `<ray-app-bar>` (RayAppBar, extends RayElement)

It follows the scroller of its ray-app-shell, else scroll-target, else the window; clear of the notch (safe-area inset). The title is plain text: put a heading in the default slot when the page needs one.

Properties:

- `label`: string. The title.
- `description`: string. A line under the title.
- `center`: boolean, reflects. The title centered (iOS).
- `variant`: `default` | `filled` | `transparent`, default `default`, reflects. default: the page background; filled: the primary color; transparent: until it elevates.
- `size`: `sm` | `md` | `lg`, default `md`, reflects. Height: 48, 56 or 64 px.
- `scrollBehavior` (attribute `scroll-behavior`): `elevate` | `hide` | `none`, default `elevate`, reflects. While the content scrolls: elevate (border and shadow), hide (also slides away going down, back going up), none.
- `sticky`: boolean, reflects. Sticks to the top of the window (outside a shell).
- `scrollTarget` (attribute `scroll-target`): string. A selector of the element whose scrolling it follows (default: its shell's, else the window).

Slots:

- (default): Title content after the label (a heading, a select).
- `start`: Before the title: back or menu button.
- `end`: Actions.
- `bottom`: A row under the bar: tabs, a search field.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `bar`: The bar.
- `start`: The start area.
- `title`: The title area.
- `end`: The actions area.
- `bottom`: The row under the bar.

Methods and properties:

- `readonly concealed: boolean`: Whether scroll-behavior="hide" has slid it away.

### App shell

The frame of an app (Mantine's AppShell): header, navbar, main, aside and footer on wide screens; on phones one column with a bottom bar. The main content scrolls, the bars stay.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/app-shell";` · Category: Layout

#### `<ray-app-shell>` (RayAppShell, extends RayElement)

The layout follows the shell's own width (a phone-sized frame shows the phone layout). Below breakpoint the navbar and the aside take no room (a ray-sidebar there still opens as its drawer) and the bottom slot shows. It fills the window's height (100dvh) unless sized. In a std/ui full_content window (ray-elements/core/raylang.js) the header becomes the title bar: room for the window buttons, and it drags the window; with layout="alt" or no header, the navbar and main start below it.

Properties:

- `layout`: `default` | `alt`, default `default`, reflects. default: the header across the top; alt: the navbar full height, the header beside it.
- `breakpoint`: string, default `48em`. Width (px, em or rem) below which it takes the phone layout.
- `padding`: string, reflects. Padding of the main area: xs…xl, a number (px) or a CSS length.

Events:

- `ray-breakpoint` (detail `{ mobile: boolean }`): It switched between the wide and the phone layout.

Slots:

- (default): The main content (it scrolls).
- `header`: Top bar: a ray-app-bar or a header of your own.
- `navbar`: Side navigation (a ray-sidebar). Wide screens only.
- `aside`: A panel on the other side (details, an inspector). Wide screens only.
- `footer`: Under the main content.
- `bottom`: Phones only: a ray-bottom-nav.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `shell`: The grid.
- `header`: The header area.
- `navbar`: The navbar area.
- `main`: The scrolling main area.
- `aside`: The aside area.
- `footer`: The footer area.
- `bottom`: The bottom bar area.

Methods and properties:

- `readonly scroller: HTMLElement`: The element that scrolls the main content.
- `readonly mobile: boolean`: Whether it is in the phone layout.

#### In a raylang app

In a `std/ui` window opened as `full_content` (the page under a transparent title bar, macOS), with [the native bridge](https://elements.raylang.dev/raylang.html#using-the-bridge), the header becomes the title bar: at least as tall, with room for the window buttons, and dragging it moves the window (buttons in it stay buttons). With `layout="alt"` or without a header, the navbar and the main content start below the title bar.

```ray
var o = ui.options(1100, 720);
o.kind = "full_content";
let h = ui.open_with("Builds", "ray://app/index.html", o)?;
```

The bridge also keeps the window's background and title bar in the theme's background, so switching to dark, resizing or reopening never flashes the other theme.

### Aspect ratio

A box with a fixed width/height ratio; its image, video or iframe fills it.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/aspect-ratio";` · Category: Layout

#### `<ray-aspect-ratio>` (RayAspectRatio, extends RayElement)

Properties:

- `ratio`: string, default `16/9`, reflects. Width/height: "16/9", "4:3", "1" or a number.
- `fit`: `cover` | `contain`, default `cover`, reflects. How the media fills the box (object-fit).
- `radius`: string, reflects. Corner radius: xs…xl, full or a CSS length.

Slots:

- (default): The media (img, video, iframe or any element); it fills the box.

Exports (from `@raylang/elements/aspect-ratio` and `@raylang/elements`):

- `function parseRatio(value: string | number): string | null`: A ratio ("16/9", "4:3", 1.5) as a CSS aspect-ratio value, or null.

### Card

A surface for grouped content, with optional media, header and footer.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/card";` · Category: Layout

#### `<ray-card>` (RayCard, extends RayElement)

Properties:

- `padding`: `0` | `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`, default `md`, reflects. Inner spacing (named space scale).
- `radius`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`. Corner radius. Default: --ray-radius-default.
- `shadow`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`. Elevation.
- `withBorder` (attribute `with-border`): boolean. Draws a border.
- `variant`: `default` | `filled` | `outline`, default `default`, reflects. default: card surface; filled: muted surface; outline: border without fill.

Slots:

- (default): The body.
- `media`: Full-bleed image or media at the top.
- `header`: Header content.
- `footer`: Footer content (actions).

Parts (`::part()`):

- `card`: The surface.
- `header`: The header area.
- `body`: The body area.
- `footer`: The footer area.

### Center

Its content centered on both axes (Mantine's Center): empty states, loaders, a sign-in card.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/center";` · Category: Layout

#### `<ray-center>` (RayCenter, extends RayElement)

It fills its parent's width; give it a height (or a flex or grid parent that stretches it) to center vertically.

Properties:

- `inline`: boolean, reflects. As wide as its content (inline-flex): an icon beside text.

Slots:

- (default): The content.

### Container

Its content centered, up to a maximum width, with side padding (Mantine's Container): the column of a page.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/container";` · Category: Layout

#### `<ray-container>` (RayContainer, extends RayElement)

Properties:

- `size`: string, default `md`, reflects. Maximum width: xs 540px, sm 720px, md 960px, lg 1140px, xl 1320px, or any CSS length.
- `padding`: string, default `md`, reflects. Side padding: xs…xl, a number (px) or a CSS length.
- `fluid`: boolean, reflects. No maximum width: the whole width, still padded.

Slots:

- (default): The content.

Exports (from `@raylang/elements/container` and `@raylang/elements`):

- `const CONTAINER_SIZES: { xs: string; sm: string; md: string; lg: string; xl: string }`: The maximum widths of size.

### Grid

A responsive grid: a column count per width (cols="1 sm:2 lg:4") measured on the grid itself, or as many columns of a minimum width as fit. Children span columns with data-span.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/grid";` · Category: Layout

#### `<ray-grid>` (RayGrid, extends RayElement)

The widths are the grid's own (container queries: xs 36em, sm 48em, md 62em, lg 75em, xl 88em), so a grid in a narrow column or a phone frame drops to fewer columns. It needs a width from its parent: in a flex row give it one or let it grow. A child spans with data-span="2"…"12" or "full".

Properties:

- `cols`: string, default `1`, reflects. Columns: a count, then counts from a width up ("1 sm:2 lg:4").
- `minColWidth` (attribute `min-col-width`): string. Instead of cols: as many columns of at least this width as fit ("14rem", 220).
- `gap`: string, default `md`, reflects. Space between cells: xs…xl, a number (px) or a CSS length.
- `rowGap` (attribute `row-gap`): string. Space between rows when it differs from gap.
- `align`: `stretch` | `start` | `center` | `end`, default `stretch`, reflects. Vertical alignment of the cells in a row.

Slots:

- (default): The cells (data-span="2" or "full" to span).

Parts (`::part()`):

- `grid`: The grid element.

Exports (from `@raylang/elements/grid` and `@raylang/elements`):

- `function parseCols(value: string | number | undefined): { base?: number; xs?: number; sm?: number; md?: number; lg?: number; xl?: number }`: "1 sm:2 lg:4" as counts per width.
- `const BREAKPOINTS: { xs: string; sm: string; md: string; lg: string; xl: string }`: The widths of cols (36em, 48em, 62em, 75em, 88em).

### Group

Its children in a row (Mantine's Group): spaced by the space scale, centered, wrapping when they do not fit. Toolbars, form actions, chips.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/group";` · Category: Layout

#### `<ray-group>` (RayGroup, extends RayElement)

A flex row on the host: the children are laid out directly, no wrapper.

Properties:

- `gap`: string, default `md`, reflects. Space between children: xs…xl (the space scale), a number (px) or any CSS length.
- `align`: `center` | `start` | `end` | `stretch` | `baseline`, default `center`, reflects. Cross-axis alignment.
- `justify`: `start` | `center` | `end` | `space-between` | `space-around` | `space-evenly`, default `start`, reflects. Main-axis distribution: space-between for a title on one side and actions on the other.
- `nowrap`: boolean, reflects. Keeps the children on one line.
- `grow`: boolean, reflects. The children share the width equally.

Slots:

- (default): The children.

### Scroll area

A box that scrolls its content with the native scrolling and a thin themed scrollbar (Mantine's ScrollArea). Edge shadows tell there is more; ray-reach-end fires at the end (load the next page).

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/scroll-area";` · Category: Layout

#### `<ray-scroll-area>` (RayScrollArea, extends RayElement)

Give it a size: height, max-height, CSS, or a flex/grid parent. The scrolling box is focusable (keyboard scrolling); name it with label when it holds a region of its own.

Properties:

- `height`: string. Height (CSS length).
- `maxHeight` (attribute `max-height`): string. Maximum height: it grows with its content up to this, then scrolls.
- `orientation`: `vertical` | `horizontal` | `both`, default `vertical`, reflects. Which ways it scrolls.
- `type`: `auto` | `hover` | `never`, default `auto`, reflects. The scrollbar: auto (when it scrolls), hover (while hovered or scrolling), never (still scrolls).
- `noShadows` (attribute `no-shadows`): boolean, reflects. No edge shadows.
- `threshold`: number, default `48`. Distance from the end (px) at which ray-reach-end fires.
- `label`: string. Accessible name: makes the scrolling box a named region.

Events:

- `ray-reach-end` (detail `{ edge: "bottom" | "right" | "left" }`): The end came within threshold (once per arrival): the bottom, or the right when horizontal (the left right to left).

Slots:

- (default): The content.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `viewport`: The scrolling box.
- `shadow`: The edge shadows.

Methods and properties:

- `readonly viewport: HTMLElement`: The scrolling element (scrollTop, scrollTo…).
- `scrollToStart(options?: { behavior?: ScrollBehavior }): void`: Scrolls to the start: the top, or the left when horizontal (the right right to left).
- `scrollToEnd(options?: { behavior?: ScrollBehavior }): void`: Scrolls to the end: the bottom, or the right when horizontal (the left right to left).

### Separator

A horizontal or vertical rule, optionally labeled (Mantine's Divider).

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/separator";` · Category: Layout

#### `<ray-separator>` (RaySeparator, extends RayElement)

Properties:

- `orientation`: `horizontal` | `vertical`, default `horizontal`, reflects. Direction of the rule.
- `label`: string, reflects. Text in the middle of a horizontal rule.
- `labelPosition` (attribute `label-position`): `start` | `center` | `end` | `left` | `right`, default `center`, reflects. Where the label sits: start/end follow the writing direction; left/right are sides of the screen.
- `size`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`, default `xs`, reflects. Thickness (1–5px).
- `variant`: `solid` | `dashed` | `dotted`, default `solid`, reflects. Line style.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `line`: The rule without label.
- `label`: The labeled rule.

### Split

Two panes with a draggable, keyboard-accessible divider (window splitter pattern); the size can be remembered.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/split";` · Category: Layout

#### `<ray-split>` (RaySplit, extends RayElement)

Divider keys: arrows move it (Shift: faster), Home/End go to min/max, Enter or double click collapse the start pane.

Properties:

- `orientation`: `horizontal` | `vertical`, default `horizontal`, reflects. horizontal: side by side; vertical: stacked.
- `position`: string, default `50%`. Initial size of the start pane: px (280) or any CSS length (30%, 20rem).
- `min`: number, default `0`. Minimum size of the start pane in px.
- `max`: number. Maximum size of the start pane in px.
- `collapsed`: boolean, reflects. The start pane is hidden.
- `disabled`: boolean, reflects. The divider cannot be moved.
- `autosave`: string. A key: the size is saved in localStorage and restored.

Events:

- `ray-resize` (detail `{ size: number; collapsed: boolean }`): After a drag, a key or a collapse.

Slots:

- `start`: The sized pane (sidebar).
- `end`: The pane that takes the rest.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `divider`: The separator.
- `start`: The start pane.
- `end`: The end pane.

Methods and properties:

- `readonly size: number`: The start pane's size in px.
- `toggle(): void`: Collapses or restores the start pane.

### Stack

Its children in a column, spaced by the space scale (Mantine's Stack): forms, panels, anything stacked.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/stack";` · Category: Layout

#### `<ray-stack>` (RayStack, extends RayElement)

A flex column on the host: the children are laid out directly, no wrapper.

Properties:

- `gap`: string, default `md`, reflects. Space between children: xs…xl (the space scale), a number (px) or any CSS length.
- `align`: `stretch` | `start` | `center` | `end` | `baseline`, default `stretch`, reflects. Cross-axis alignment: stretch fills the width.
- `justify`: `start` | `center` | `end` | `space-between` | `space-around` | `space-evenly`, default `start`, reflects. Main-axis distribution (with a height to distribute).

Slots:

- (default): The children.

Exports (from `@raylang/elements/stack` and `@raylang/elements`):

- `function applyFlex(el: HTMLElement, options: { gap?: string; align?: string; justify?: string }, alignDefault: string): void`: Gap, align and justify of a stack or group onto an element's custom properties (for a layout component of your own).

### Status bar

The bar at the bottom of an app window: items on the left and on the right; items with action are buttons.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/statusbar";` · Category: Layout

#### `<ray-statusbar>` (RayStatusbar, extends RayElement)

Properties:

- `variant`: `default` | `accent`, default `default`, reflects. accent: the primary color (e.g. while debugging).

Slots:

- (default): Items on the left.
- `right`: Items on the right.

#### `<ray-statusbar-item>` (RayStatusbarItem, extends RayElement)

Properties:

- `action`: boolean, reflects. A button (listen to click).
- `color`: string, reflects. Text color (red for errors…).
- `label`: string. Accessible name and tooltip (for icon-only or terse items).

Slots:

- (default): Text.
- `icon`: Icon.

### Theme toggle

Icon button that cycles the document theme: system, light, dark.

Import: `import "@raylang/elements/theme-toggle";` · Category: Theme

#### `<ray-theme-toggle>` (RayThemeToggle, extends RayElement)

Properties:

- `size`: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`, default `sm`, reflects. Control height.

Events:

- `ray-theme-change` (detail `{ theme: "light" | "dark" | "system"; resolved: "light" | "dark"; primary: string | null }`): Fired on the document root by setTheme(); detail: { theme, resolved, primary }.

Parts (`::part()`):

- `button`: The inner button.

## Tokens

Use them as `var(--ray-…)` in your own CSS. Values are resolved; the semantic ones change with the theme (light / dark).

- Palette: `--ray-<color>-0` (lightest) … `--ray-<color>-9` (darkest), colors `dark`, `gray`, `red`, `pink`, `violet`, `indigo`, `blue`, `cyan`, `teal`, `green`, `yellow`, `orange`. The same in both themes.
- Per color and for `primary`: `--ray-<color>-<variant>`, variants `filled`, `filled-hover`, `light`, `light-hover`, `light-color`, `outline`, `outline-hover`, `contrast`; theme-aware.
- Primary: `--ray-primary-0` … `-9` and its variants, aliases of the primary color (`blue`; `data-primary` or `setPrimary()` changes it).

base:

- `--ray-white`: #ffffff
- `--ray-black`: #000000

semantic:

- `--ray-background`: #ffffff / #141414
- `--ray-foreground`: #212529 / #f1f3f5
- `--ray-card`: #ffffff / #1f1f1f
- `--ray-card-foreground`: #212529 / #f1f3f5
- `--ray-popover`: #ffffff / #1f1f1f
- `--ray-popover-foreground`: #212529 / #f1f3f5
- `--ray-primary`: #1971c2
- `--ray-primary-hover`: #1864ab
- `--ray-primary-foreground`: #ffffff
- `--ray-secondary`: #f1f3f5 / #2e2e2e
- `--ray-secondary-hover`: #e9ecef / #3b3b3b
- `--ray-secondary-foreground`: #212529 / #f1f3f5
- `--ray-default`: #ffffff / color-mix(in srgb, #ffffff 3%, transparent)

- `--ray-raised`: #ffffff / #424242
